# 0. Configuration

```{r config}
# ── Clinical axes and candidate response sets ────────────────────────────────
# The four physiological axes elicited from the clinical investigators are
# haematological, renal, hepatic and inflammatory. STAGE 1 fits all four and
# tests whether the inflammatory axis earns its parameters.
#
# Names are matched against the columns of the imputed file with a tolerant
# resolver (see `resolve_names()` in Section 2), so "CRP" will match
# "CRP (mg/L)", "CRP (mg/dL)", "PCR (mg/L)", etc. Set the exact string here
# if the resolver reports an ambiguity.
AXIS_STEMS <- c(haematological = "HGB",
                renal          = "CREA",
                hepatic        = "ALT",
                inflammatory   = "CRP (mg/L)")

# The axis dropped by STAGE 1 (kept as a config value so the notebook states
# the hypothesis explicitly rather than hard-coding the conclusion).
AXIS_UNDER_TEST <- "inflammatory"

# Number of states used for the response-set comparison of STAGE 1. Held
# fixed across response sets so the comparison is like-for-like.
K_AXIS_TEST <- 4

# Candidate state counts compared in STAGE 2 (deliberately not a full grid:
# each fit is expensive at this cohort size).
K_GRID <- c(3, 4, 5)

# ── Covariates on the OBSERVATION model (means only) ─────────────────────────
# Empty = covariate-free model. Covariates are NOT part of the thesis model:
# they are used only for cohort description and phenotype stratification.
OBS_COVARIATES <- character(0)

# ── Z-score normalisation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
APPLY_ZSCORE <- TRUE

# ── Observation model family ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# TRUE  -> full multivariate normal (state-specific covariance).
# FALSE -> independent normals per biomarker (NOT supported by the fitting
#          engine of Section 3; the thesis model is the MVN one).
IS_a_MVN <- TRUE

# ── Per-covariate term specification (unused while OBS_COVARIATES is empty) ──
SPLINE_K_DEFAULT <- 8
SPLINE_BS        <- "cs"
COVARIATE_TERMS  <- list("HGB (g/dL)"   = "linear",
                         "CREA (mg/dL)" = "linear",
                         "ALT (U/L)"    = "linear")

# ── Random seed ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SEED <- 10

# ── NO TRAIN / TEST SPLIT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Every model in this notebook is fitted on the FULL cohort of its stage.
# The held-out-patient experiment of the previous version is removed: the
# thesis reports no out-of-sample analysis, and the 5% hold-out made the
# estimation cohort (987) inconsistent with the cohort described in
# Chapter 1 (1039). Kept as a frozen constant only so the export bundle
# schema stays backwards compatible with hmm_posthoc.Rmd.
TEST_FRAC <- 0

# ── File paths ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SPEC_* : CRP/WBC-inclusive imputed cohort. Required by STAGE 1, because the
#          inflammatory axis only exists in this file.
SPEC_DATA_PATH      <- "df_imputed_wide_log1p_HgbCreaAltWbcCrp.csv"
SPEC_DECISIONS_PATH <- "bm_log1p_decisions_HgbCreaAltWbcCrp.csv"

# FULL_* : the HGB/CREA/ALT imputed cohort described in Chapter 1.
FULL_DATA_PATH      <- "df_imputed_wide_log1p_HgbCreaAlt.csv"
FULL_DECISIONS_PATH <- "bm_log1p_decisions_HgbCreaAlt.csv"

# Clinical reference intervals extracted by Final_pipeline.ipynb.
REF_RANGES_PATH     <- "biomarker_reference_ranges.csv"

# ── Which cohort carries each stage ──────────────────────────────────────────
# STAGE 1 always runs on the CRP/WBC-inclusive cohort (it has to).
#
# K_SELECTION_COHORT and FINAL_COHORT:
#   "full" -> the Chapter-1 cohort (FULL_DATA_PATH)
#   "spec" -> the CRP/WBC-inclusive subcohort (SPEC_DATA_PATH)
#
# Default "full": K and the final model are properties of the model reported
# in the thesis, and that model is fitted on the cohort Chapter 1 describes.
# The CRP/WBC subcohort then enters the thesis only as the (smaller, nested)
# sample on which the response set was chosen, which is stated once in
# Section 3.3 of the chapter. Set both to "spec" to run every stage on the
# CRP/WBC cohort instead.
K_SELECTION_COHORT <- "full"
FINAL_COHORT       <- "full"

# ── Clinical state labels for the FINAL model only ───────────────────────────
# Assigned automatically in Section 5.2 from the estimated state means, then
# printed for verification. Nothing here is applied to the candidate models
# of Sections 3A / 3B.
#
# Rule (K = 4): the state with the highest creatinine mean is "Renal", the
# state with the highest ALT mean among the rest is "Hepatic", the state
# with the lowest haemoglobin mean among the rest is "Anaemic", and the
# remaining state is "Stable". The previous label "Weak state" is retired:
# it conflated the anaemia-dominant and the hepatic states.
STATE_LABEL_ORDER   <- c("Stable state", "Anaemic state",
                         "Hepatic state", "Renal state")
STATE_PALETTE_CUSTOM <- c(
  "#579D1CFF",   # Stable state
  "#004586FF",   # Anaemic state
  "#FF950EFF",   # Hepatic state
  "#C5000BFF"    # Renal state
)
# Set to a named list ("1" = "...", ...) to override the automatic assignment.
STATE_LABELS_MAP_OVERRIDE <- NULL

# ── Smoke test ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# > 0 keeps only the first SMOKE_TEST_N patients of each file, so the whole
# notebook can be knitted end to end in minutes to check that it runs.
# ALWAYS set back to 0 before producing anything for the thesis: every number
# and every figure produced under a smoke test is meaningless.
SMOKE_TEST_N <- 0

# ── Output directory for figures and tables ──────────────────────────────────
FIG_DIR <- "figures"

# Derived flag
has_covariates <- length(OBS_COVARIATES) > 0
cat("Covariate-augmented observation model:", has_covariates, "\n")
if (has_covariates) cat("Covariates:", paste(OBS_COVARIATES, collapse = ", "), "\n")
stopifnot(IS_a_MVN)
```

## 1.1 Figure and table export helpers

Every figure and table referenced by Chapter 3 is written to `FIG_DIR` as a
file, so the thesis includes artefacts produced by this run and not
screenshots.

```{r export-helpers}
dir.create(FIG_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Save a ggplot / patchwork object as PNG (+ PDF for LaTeX inclusion).
save_fig <- function(plot, name, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300) {
  png_path <- file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".png"))
  pdf_path <- file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".pdf"))
  ggplot2::ggsave(png_path, plot = plot, width = width, height = height,
                  dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
  try(ggplot2::ggsave(pdf_path, plot = plot, width = width, height = height,
                      device = cairo_pdf, bg = "white"), silent = TRUE)
  cat("[figure] ", png_path, "\n", sep = "")
  invisible(png_path)
}

# Save a data frame as CSV and echo it into the knitted document.
save_tab <- function(df, name, caption = NULL, digits = 3) {
  csv_path <- file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".csv"))
  readr::write_csv(df, csv_path)
  cat("[table]  ", csv_path, "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(caption)) cat(caption, "\n", sep = "")
  print(as.data.frame(df |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                                                        \(x) round(x, digits)))),
        row.names = FALSE)
  invisible(csv_path)
}
```

# 2. Data preparation engine

The previous version of this notebook hard-wired one data file and one
response set into the top-level chunks. Two cohorts are now needed (the
CRP/WBC-inclusive one for the response-set comparison, the Chapter-1 one for
the final model), so the whole load-and-preprocess block is wrapped in a
single function and called once per cohort. The body is the original code of
Sections 2 and 3.1--3.5, unchanged in substance: sequential patient IDs,
mgcv-safe column names, z-scoring with stored parameters, log1p
back-transform decisions, and the clinical reference intervals.

## 2.1 Reference intervals (cohort-independent)

```{r reference-intervals-global}
if (file.exists(REF_RANGES_PATH)) {
  ref_raw <- readr::read_csv(REF_RANGES_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(lln), !is.na(uln), uln > lln)

  if (any(ref_raw$n_distinct_ranges > 1))
    message("Reference ranges resolved from multiple clinician-entered variants ",
            "(weighted average) for: ",
            paste(ref_raw$biomarker[ref_raw$n_distinct_ranges > 1], collapse = ", "))

  REF_INTERVALS <- setNames(
    Map(function(l, u) c(l, u), ref_raw$lln, ref_raw$uln),
    ref_raw$biomarker
  )
} else {
  warning("REF_RANGES_PATH not found (", REF_RANGES_PATH,
          "); reference bands/columns will be omitted.")
  REF_INTERVALS <- list()
}

# [LLN, ULN] treated as the central 95% reference interval -> mean +/- 1.96 SD.
REF_COVERAGE_Z <- 1.96

CATEGORICAL_COVS <- c("hospital_ward", "sex", "admission_reason",
                      "treatment_target", "ECOG",
                      "discharge_mode", "discharge_dead", "discharged_alive",
                      "admission_start_date", "admission_end_date",
                      "solid_tumor_category", "discharge_mortality_90d")
```

## 2.2 The preparation function

```{r prep-function}
# Resolve a biomarker stem ("CRP") to the actual column name in a data set
# ("CRP (mg/L)"). Errors loudly on 0 or >1 matches rather than guessing.
resolve_names <- function(stems, available) {
  vapply(stems, function(s) {
    hit <- available[startsWith(toupper(available), toupper(s))]
    if (length(hit) == 0)
      stop("Biomarker stem '", s, "' matches no column. Available: ",
           paste(available, collapse = " | "))
    if (length(hit) > 1)
      stop("Biomarker stem '", s, "' is ambiguous, matches: ",
           paste(hit, collapse = " | "),
           ". Put the exact column name in AXIS_STEMS.")
    hit
  }, character(1))
}

build_analysis_data <- function(data_path, decisions_path, axis_stems,
                                label = basename(data_path)) {

  if (!file.exists(data_path))
    stop("Data file not found: ", data_path)
  if (!file.exists(decisions_path))
    stop("log1p-decisions file not found: ", decisions_path)

  df_raw <- readr::read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

  if (SMOKE_TEST_N > 0) {
    keep_ids <- head(sort(unique(df_raw$patient_id)), SMOKE_TEST_N)
    df_raw <- df_raw[df_raw$patient_id %in% keep_ids, , drop = FALSE]
    cat("*** SMOKE TEST: ", data_path, " truncated to ", length(keep_ids),
        " patients. Results are NOT usable. ***\n", sep = "")
  }

  # ---- column groups (identical to the original Section 2) ----------------
  cov_cols <- c(
    "admission_start_date", "admission_end_date",
    "sex", "hospital_ward", "age", "pack_years_smoking", "alcohol_years",
    "length_of_stay_days", "days_in_ER", "ER_last_day",
    "admissions_last_12m", "admissions_last_6m",
    "ECOG", "Barthel_index", "Braden_score", "CIRS_total_score",
    "admission_reason", "discharge_dead", "discharge_mode", "discharged_alive",
    "solid_tumor_category",
    "date_of_death", "is_dead",
    "discharge_mortality_90d", "days_death_from_admission",
    "days_death_from_discharge"
  )
  id_cols  <- c("patient_id", "analysis_date", "day")
  bio_cols <- setdiff(names(df_raw), c(id_cols, cov_cols))

  df_raw <- df_raw |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(intersect(CATEGORICAL_COVS, names(df_raw))), as.factor))

  # ---- resolve the requested axes to real column names --------------------
  RESPONSE_VARS <- unname(resolve_names(axis_stems, bio_cols))
  names(RESPONSE_VARS) <- names(axis_stems)

  missing_cov <- setdiff(OBS_COVARIATES, names(df_raw))
  if (length(missing_cov) > 0)
    stop("Configured covariates not found in ", label, ": ",
         paste(missing_cov, collapse = ", "))

  patient_ids <- sort(unique(df_raw$patient_id))

  cat("\n== Cohort: ", label, " ==\n", sep = "")
  cat("  file                  : ", data_path, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  rows                  : ", nrow(df_raw), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  patients              : ", length(patient_ids), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  days                  : ", dplyr::n_distinct(df_raw$day),
      " (", min(df_raw$day), "..", max(df_raw$day), ")\n", sep = "")
  cat("  biomarker columns     : ", length(bio_cols), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  response variables    : ", paste(RESPONSE_VARS, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")

  # ---- sequential patient ID (original Section 3.1) -----------------------
  patient_map <- df_raw |>
    dplyr::distinct(patient_id) |>
    dplyr::arrange(patient_id) |>
    dplyr::mutate(ID = as.factor(dplyr::row_number()))

  df <- df_raw |>
    dplyr::left_join(patient_map, by = "patient_id") |>
    dplyr::relocate(ID, .before = 1) |>
    dplyr::arrange(ID, day) |>
    dplyr::rename(time = day)

  id_lookup <- df |> dplyr::distinct(ID, patient_id)
  df <- df |> dplyr::select(-patient_id)

  # ---- mgcv-safe names (original Section 3.2) -----------------------------
  make_safe_names <- function(orig) {
    if (length(orig) == 0) return(character(0))
    base <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", orig)
    base <- gsub("^_+|_+$", "", base)
    base[base == ""] <- "var"
    make.unique(paste0("v_", base), sep = "_")
  }
  all_orig        <- c(unname(RESPONSE_VARS), OBS_COVARIATES)
  all_safe        <- make_safe_names(all_orig)
  display_to_safe <- setNames(all_safe, all_orig)
  safe_to_display <- setNames(all_orig, all_safe)

  rename_vec <- setNames(names(display_to_safe), as.character(display_to_safe))
  df <- df |> dplyr::rename(!!!rename_vec)

  RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE  <- unname(display_to_safe[unname(RESPONSE_VARS)])
  names(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE) <- names(RESPONSE_VARS)
  OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE <- unname(display_to_safe[OBS_COVARIATES])

  display     <- function(safe_name)  unname(safe_to_display[safe_name])
  display_vec <- function(safe_names) unname(safe_to_display[safe_names])

  # ---- z-scoring (original Section 3.3) -----------------------------------
  numeric_covariates_safe <- OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE[
    vapply(OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE, function(s) is.numeric(df[[s]]), logical(1))
  ]
  cols_to_zscore <- c(unname(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE), numeric_covariates_safe)

  zscore_params <- df |>
    dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(cols_to_zscore),
      list(mean = \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = \(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .names = "{.col}__{.fn}")) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(),
                        names_to = c("biomarker", ".value"), names_sep = "__")

  if (APPLY_ZSCORE) {
    df <- df |>
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(cols_to_zscore),
        ~ (. - mean(., na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(., na.rm = TRUE)))
    cat("  z-score applied to    : ",
        paste(unname(RESPONSE_VARS), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  }

  inv_zscore <- function(z_vals, biomarker_safe) {
    if (!APPLY_ZSCORE) return(z_vals)
    row <- zscore_params[zscore_params$biomarker == biomarker_safe, ]
    z_vals * row$sd + row$mean
  }

  # ---- log1p decisions (original Section 3.4) -----------------------------
  bm_decisions <- readr::read_csv(decisions_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::filter(biomarker %in% unname(RESPONSE_VARS)) |>
    dplyr::select(biomarker, apply_log1p)

  bm_decisions$biomarker_safe <- display_to_safe[bm_decisions$biomarker]
  needs_expm1 <- setNames(bm_decisions$apply_log1p, bm_decisions$biomarker_safe)
  # Any response variable absent from the decisions file is treated as
  # untransformed, and that is reported rather than silently assumed.
  absent <- setdiff(unname(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE), names(needs_expm1))
  if (length(absent) > 0) {
    warning("No log1p decision found for: ",
            paste(display_vec(absent), collapse = ", "),
            " -- treated as untransformed.")
    for (a in absent) needs_expm1[[a]] <- FALSE
  }
  cat("  log1p-transformed     : ",
      paste(display_vec(names(needs_expm1))[unlist(needs_expm1)],
            collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")

  to_clinical <- function(values, biomarker_safe) {
    v <- inv_zscore(values, biomarker_safe)
    if (isTRUE(needs_expm1[[biomarker_safe]])) v <- expm1(v)
    v
  }

  to_clinical_sd <- function(sd_values, biomarker_safe, mu_logscale = NULL) {
    s <- sd_values
    if (APPLY_ZSCORE) {
      row <- zscore_params[zscore_params$biomarker == biomarker_safe, ]
      s <- s * row$sd
    }
    if (isTRUE(needs_expm1[[biomarker_safe]])) {
      if (is.null(mu_logscale))
        stop("to_clinical_sd(): `mu_logscale` required for log1p biomarker '",
             display(biomarker_safe), "'.")
      mu_log <- if (APPLY_ZSCORE) {
        row <- zscore_params[zscore_params$biomarker == biomarker_safe, ]
        mu_logscale * row$sd + row$mean
      } else mu_logscale
      var_clin <- (exp(s^2) - 1) * exp(2 * mu_log + s^2)
      s <- sqrt(var_clin)
    }
    s
  }

  axis_label <- function(biomarker_safe) {
    disp <- display(biomarker_safe)
    bits <- character()
    if (isTRUE(needs_expm1[[biomarker_safe]])) bits <- c(bits, "back-transformed from log1p")
    if (APPLY_ZSCORE)                          bits <- c(bits, "model on z-scores")
    if (length(bits) == 0) disp else paste0(disp, " (", paste(bits, collapse = "; "), ")")
  }

  global_scale_subtitle <- function() {
    any_log1p <- any(unlist(needs_expm1))
    if (any_log1p && APPLY_ZSCORE)
      "Clinical scale (back-transformed from z-score and log1p where applicable)"
    else if (any_log1p) "Clinical scale (back-transformed from log1p where applicable)"
    else if (APPLY_ZSCORE) "Clinical scale (back-transformed from z-score)"
    else "Raw input scale"
  }

  # ---- reference-interval helpers (original Section 3.4b) -----------------
  ref_mean_sd <- function(display_name) {
    iv <- REF_INTERVALS[[display_name]]
    if (is.null(iv)) return(NULL)
    list(mean = mean(iv), sd = (iv[2] - iv[1]) / (2 * REF_COVERAGE_Z),
         lln = iv[1], uln = iv[2])
  }
  ref_by_safe <- function(biomarker_safe) ref_mean_sd(display(biomarker_safe))

  to_model <- function(x_clin, biomarker_safe) {
    x <- if (isTRUE(needs_expm1[[biomarker_safe]])) log1p(x_clin) else x_clin
    if (APPLY_ZSCORE) {
      row <- zscore_params[zscore_params$biomarker == biomarker_safe, ]
      x <- (x - row$mean) / row$sd
    }
    x
  }

  list(
    label = label, data_path = data_path,
    df = df, bio_cols = bio_cols, id_lookup = id_lookup,
    patient_ids = patient_ids,
    n_patients = length(patient_ids), n_rows = nrow(df),
    RESPONSE_VARS = RESPONSE_VARS, RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE = RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE,
    OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE = OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE,
    display_to_safe = display_to_safe, safe_to_display = safe_to_display,
    display = display, display_vec = display_vec,
    zscore_params = zscore_params, inv_zscore = inv_zscore,
    needs_expm1 = needs_expm1,
    to_clinical = to_clinical, to_clinical_sd = to_clinical_sd,
    axis_label = axis_label, global_scale_subtitle = global_scale_subtitle,
    ref_mean_sd = ref_mean_sd, ref_by_safe = ref_by_safe, to_model = to_model
  )
}

# Promote one prepared cohort to the global names used by Sections 4-12.
# Everything downstream of the final fit reads these globals, exactly as in
# the original notebook.
use_dataset <- function(D, response_safe = NULL) {
  keep <- c("df", "bio_cols", "RESPONSE_VARS", "RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE",
            "OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE", "display_to_safe", "safe_to_display",
            "display", "display_vec", "zscore_params", "inv_zscore",
            "needs_expm1", "to_clinical", "to_clinical_sd", "axis_label",
            "global_scale_subtitle", "ref_mean_sd", "ref_by_safe", "to_model",
            "id_lookup")
  list2env(D[keep], envir = globalenv())
  if (!is.null(response_safe)) {
    assign("RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE", unname(response_safe), envir = globalenv())
    assign("RESPONSE_VARS",
           unname(D$safe_to_display[response_safe]), envir = globalenv())
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

## 2.3 Build the cohorts

```{r build-cohorts}
AXIS_FINAL <- setdiff(names(AXIS_STEMS), AXIS_UNDER_TEST)

data_spec <- build_analysis_data(
  SPEC_DATA_PATH, SPEC_DECISIONS_PATH, AXIS_STEMS,
  label = "CRP/WBC-inclusive (4 axes)")

have_full <- file.exists(FULL_DATA_PATH) && file.exists(FULL_DECISIONS_PATH)
if (have_full) {
  data_full <- build_analysis_data(
    FULL_DATA_PATH, FULL_DECISIONS_PATH, AXIS_STEMS[AXIS_FINAL],
    label = "Chapter-1 cohort (3 axes)")
} else {
  data_full <- NULL
  warning("FULL_DATA_PATH / FULL_DECISIONS_PATH not found. ",
          "K selection and the final model will fall back to the ",
          "CRP/WBC-inclusive cohort.")
  K_SELECTION_COHORT <- "spec"
  FINAL_COHORT       <- "spec"
}

pick_cohort <- function(which) if (identical(which, "spec") || is.null(data_full)) data_spec else data_full
```

## 2.4 Cohort reconciliation

The two imputed files do not describe the same patients: requiring CRP and
WBC to satisfy the sparsity criterion removes patients that the Chapter-1
cohort retains. This is reported explicitly, because it determines what the
response-set comparison of Section 3A can and cannot claim about the cohort
of the final model.

```{r cohort-reconciliation}
if (!is.null(data_full)) {
```

# 3. Model fitting engine

One function fits one candidate model. Sections 3A and 3B call it; Section 5
calls it once more for the final model. The construction is exactly the one
used previously (stationary initial distribution, $k$-means starting values
for the multivariate-normal emissions, diagonally dominant starting
transition matrix, fixed seed), lifted out of the top-level chunks so that
every candidate is fitted under identical conditions.

```{r fit-engine}
# ---- data frame in hmmTMB shape, for a given response set -----------------
make_hmm_data <- function(D, resp_safe) {
  keep_cols <- c("ID", "time", unname(resp_safe), D$OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE)
  hd <- D$df |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(keep_cols)) |>
    dplyr::arrange(ID, time)
  hd$z <- asplit(as.matrix(hd[, unname(resp_safe), drop = FALSE]), 1)
  hd
}

# ---- k-means starting values for the MVN emissions ------------------------
kmeans_init <- function(hd, resp_safe, K, seed = SEED, verbose = FALSE,
                        jitter_sd = 0) {
  n_vars <- length(resp_safe)
  set.seed(seed)
  km_data <- as.matrix(hd[, unname(resp_safe), drop = FALSE])
  km_data <- km_data[complete.cases(km_data), , drop = FALSE]
  km <- kmeans(km_data, centers = K, nstart = 25)

  # Order centres by the first response so re-runs are reproducible.
  ord     <- order(km$centers[, 1])
  centers <- km$centers[ord, , drop = FALSE]

  cluster_assign <- km$cluster
  sds        <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = K, ncol = n_vars)
  corrs_list <- vector("list", K)
  for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    idx <- which(cluster_assign == ord[k])
    if (length(idx) >= 2) {
      sub <- km_data[idx, , drop = FALSE]
      sds[k, ] <- apply(sub, 2, sd)
      corrs_list[[k]] <- cov2cor(cov(sub))
    } else {
      sds[k, ] <- apply(km_data, 2, sd)
      corrs_list[[k]] <- diag(n_vars)
    }
  }
  global_sd <- apply(km_data, 2, sd)
  for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    bad <- is.na(sds[k, ]) | sds[k, ] <= 0
    sds[k, bad] <- global_sd[bad]
  }

  # Genuine perturbation of the starting point. Varying only the seed passed
  # to kmeans() does NOT perturb anything: with nstart = 25 the partition is
  # the same every time, so every "restart" would begin from identical values.
  if (jitter_sd > 0) {
    centers <- centers +
      matrix(rnorm(K * n_vars, 0, jitter_sd) * rep(global_sd, each = K),
             K, n_vars)
    sds <- sds * exp(matrix(rnorm(K * n_vars, 0, jitter_sd / 2), K, n_vars))
    centers <- centers[order(centers[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
  }

  par0_z <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(n_vars)) par0_z[[paste0("mu", i)]] <- centers[, i]
  for (i in seq_len(n_vars)) par0_z[[paste0("sd", i)]] <- sds[, i]
  if (n_vars >= 2) {
    prs <- which(upper.tri(matrix(0, n_vars, n_vars)), arr.ind = TRUE)
    for (k in seq_len(nrow(prs))) {
      i <- prs[k, 1]; j <- prs[k, 2]
      par0_z[[paste0("corr", i, j)]] <- sapply(corrs_list, function(R) R[i, j])
    }
  }
  if (verbose) {
    cat("Initial means from k-means (rows = responses, cols = raw states):\n")
    mu_df <- as.data.frame(t(centers))
    rownames(mu_df) <- unname(resp_safe)
    colnames(mu_df) <- paste0("raw state ", seq_len(K))
    print(round(mu_df, 3))
  }
  list(z = par0_z)
}

# ---- fit one candidate ----------------------------------------------------
fit_hmm <- function(D, resp_safe, K, seed = SEED, tag = NULL, verbose = TRUE,
                    jitter_sd = 0) {
  stopifnot(IS_a_MVN)
  tag <- tag %||% paste0(length(resp_safe), "resp_K", K)
  hd  <- make_hmm_data(D, resp_safe)

  hid  <- MarkovChain$new(data = hd, n_states = K, initial_state = "stationary")
  par0 <- kmeans_init(hd, resp_safe, K, seed = seed, verbose = verbose,
                      jitter_sd = jitter_sd)
  obs  <- Observation$new(data = hd, dists = list(z = "mvnorm"),
                          n_states = K, par = par0)
  m    <- HMM$new(obs = obs, hid = hid)

  t0 <- Sys.time()
  set.seed(seed)
  m$fit(silent = TRUE)
  secs <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))

  out <- m$out()
  if (verbose) {
    cat("\n[fit ", tag, "] convergence=", out$convergence,
        " | ", out$message,
        " | nll=", round(out$objective, 2),
        " | iters=", out$iterations,
        " | ", round(secs, 1), "s\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (!identical(out$convergence, 0L) && !identical(out$convergence, 0))
    warning("Candidate ", tag, " did not report clean convergence.")

  list(tag = tag, hmm = m, data = hd, K = K,
       resp_safe = unname(resp_safe),
       resp_disp = unname(D$safe_to_display[unname(resp_safe)]),
       cohort = D$label, seconds = secs, out = out)
}

`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
```

## 3.1 Diagnostics shared by all candidates

`candidate_state_pars()` duplicates, deliberately, the parameter-extraction
logic that Section 9.1 uses internally: the pseudo-residual implementation is
left untouched, so the model-comparison code carries its own copy rather than
reaching into it.

```{r candidate-diagnostics}
# ---- state parameters of a fitted candidate (raw state order) -------------
candidate_state_pars <- function(fit) {
  m <- fit$hmm; K <- fit$K; p <- length(fit$resp_safe)
  op <- m$par()$obspar[, , 1]
  mu <- sd <- matrix(NA_real_, K, p)
  for (i in seq_len(p)) {
    mu[, i] <- op[paste0("z.mu", i), ]
    sd[, i] <- op[paste0("z.sd", i), ]
  }
  Sigma_list <- vector("list", K)
  for (s in seq_len(K)) {
    R <- diag(p)
    if (p >= 2) {
      idx <- which(upper.tri(R), arr.ind = TRUE)
      for (k in seq_len(nrow(idx))) {
        i <- idx[k, 1]; j <- idx[k, 2]
        rho <- op[paste0("z.corr", i, j), s]
        R[i, j] <- R[j, i] <- rho
      }
    }
    Dm <- diag(sd[s, ], nrow = p)
    Sigma_list[[s]] <- Dm %*% R %*% Dm
  }
  colnames(mu) <- colnames(sd) <- fit$resp_disp
  list(mu = mu, sd = sd, Sigma = Sigma_list)
}

# ---- stationary distribution of a transition matrix -----------------------
stationary_dist <- function(tpm) {
  K <- nrow(tpm)
  A <- rbind(t(tpm - diag(K)), rep(1, K))
  b <- c(rep(0, K), 1)
  as.numeric(solve(t(A) %*% A, t(A) %*% b))
}

# ---- log-likelihood / parameter count / information criteria --------------
fit_loglik <- function(fit) {
  ll <- try(as.numeric(stats::logLik(fit$hmm)), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(ll, "try-error") || !is.finite(ll)) ll <- -fit$out$objective
  ll
}

fit_npar <- function(fit) {
  # Analytic count: K(K-1) transition parameters (rows sum to 1) + emission
  # parameters (p means + p sds + p(p-1)/2 correlations per state). The
  # initial distribution contributes NOTHING: it is constrained to the
  # stationary distribution of Gamma.
  K <- fit$K; p <- length(fit$resp_safe)
  analytic <- K * (K - 1) + K * (2 * p + p * (p - 1) / 2)
  from_aic <- (stats::AIC(fit$hmm) + 2 * fit_loglik(fit)) / 2
  if (is.finite(from_aic) && abs(from_aic - analytic) > 0.5)
    warning("Parameter count mismatch for ", fit$tag, ": analytic = ", analytic,
            ", implied by AIC = ", round(from_aic, 1))
  analytic
}

# Complete-data log-likelihood at the Viterbi path -> ICL.
fit_icl <- function(fit) {
  tryCatch({
    m <- fit$hmm; hd <- fit$data; K <- fit$K
    sp <- candidate_state_pars(fit)
    tpm   <- m$par()$tpm[, , 1]
    delta <- stationary_dist(tpm)
    vit   <- m$viterbi()
    X     <- as.matrix(hd[, fit$resp_safe, drop = FALSE])
    idlist <- split(seq_len(nrow(hd)), hd$ID)

    ll_c <- 0
    for (rows in idlist) {
      s <- vit[rows]
      ll_c <- ll_c + log(delta[s[1]])
      if (length(s) > 1)
        ll_c <- ll_c + sum(log(tpm[cbind(s[-length(s)], s[-1])]))
      for (k in unique(s)) {
        sel <- which(s == k)
        ll_c <- ll_c + sum(mvtnorm::dmvnorm(X[rows[sel], , drop = FALSE],
                                            mean = sp$mu[k, ],
                                            sigma = sp$Sigma[[k]], log = TRUE))
      }
    }
    -2 * ll_c + fit_npar(fit) * log(nrow(hd))
  }, error = function(e) { warning("ICL failed for ", fit$tag, ": ",
                                   conditionMessage(e)); NA_real_ })
}

fit_metrics <- function(fit) {
  ll <- fit_loglik(fit); np <- fit_npar(fit); n <- nrow(fit$data)
  tibble::tibble(
    model     = fit$tag,
    cohort    = fit$cohort,
    responses = paste(fit$resp_disp, collapse = " + "),
    p         = length(fit$resp_safe),
    K         = fit$K,
    n_obs     = n,
    n_patients = dplyr::n_distinct(fit$data$ID),
    logLik    = ll,
    npar      = np,
    AIC       = -2 * ll + 2 * np,
    BIC       = -2 * ll + np * log(n),
    ICL       = fit_icl(fit),
    seconds   = fit$seconds
  )
}

# ---- overlap between state-dependent marginals ----------------------------
# Overlapping coefficient of two univariate normals: the integral of the
# pointwise minimum of the two densities. 1 = identical, 0 = disjoint.
# A response variable whose states all overlap contributes parameters
# without contributing separation, which is exactly the STAGE 1 question.
ovl_normal <- function(m1, s1, m2, s2) {
  lo <- min(m1 - 8 * s1, m2 - 8 * s2)
  hi <- max(m1 + 8 * s1, m2 + 8 * s2)
  f  <- function(x) pmin(dnorm(x, m1, s1), dnorm(x, m2, s2))
  stats::integrate(f, lo, hi, subdivisions = 2000L, rel.tol = 1e-8)$value
}

overlap_table <- function(fit) {
  sp <- candidate_state_pars(fit); K <- fit$K
  prs <- t(combn(K, 2))
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(fit$resp_disp), function(i) {
    v <- purrr::map_dbl(seq_len(nrow(prs)), function(r) {
      a <- prs[r, 1]; b <- prs[r, 2]
      ovl_normal(sp$mu[a, i], sp$sd[a, i], sp$mu[b, i], sp$sd[b, i])
    })
    sep <- purrr::map_dbl(seq_len(nrow(prs)), function(r) {
      a <- prs[r, 1]; b <- prs[r, 2]
      abs(sp$mu[a, i] - sp$mu[b, i]) / sqrt((sp$sd[a, i]^2 + sp$sd[b, i]^2) / 2)
    })
    tibble::tibble(
      model         = fit$tag,
      biomarker     = fit$resp_disp[i],
      mean_overlap  = mean(v),
      min_overlap   = min(v),
      max_overlap   = max(v),
      mean_separation = mean(sep),
      max_separation  = max(sep)
    )
  })
}

overlap_pairs <- function(fit) {
  sp <- candidate_state_pars(fit); K <- fit$K
  prs <- t(combn(K, 2))
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(fit$resp_disp), function(i)
    purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(prs)), function(r) {
      a <- prs[r, 1]; b <- prs[r, 2]
      tibble::tibble(biomarker = fit$resp_disp[i],
                     state_a = paste0("S", a), state_b = paste0("S", b),
                     ovl = ovl_normal(sp$mu[a, i], sp$sd[a, i],
                                      sp$mu[b, i], sp$sd[b, i]))
    }))
}

# ---- state-dependent densities on the model (z-score) scale ---------------
# Candidate models are shown with RAW state indices: they have no clinical
# labels, and attaching any would presuppose the interpretation that only
# the final model earns.
plot_state_densities <- function(fit, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL) {
  sp  <- candidate_state_pars(fit)
  vit <- fit$hmm$viterbi()
  w   <- as.numeric(prop.table(table(factor(vit, levels = seq_len(fit$K)))))
  X   <- as.matrix(fit$data[, fit$resp_safe, drop = FALSE])

  dens <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(fit$resp_disp), function(i) {
    rng  <- range(X[, i], na.rm = TRUE)
    grid <- seq(rng[1] - 0.1 * diff(rng), rng[2] + 0.1 * diff(rng),
                length.out = 400)
    purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(fit$K), function(s)
      tibble::tibble(biomarker = fit$resp_disp[i],
                     state = paste0("State ", s),
                     x = grid,
                     density = w[s] * dnorm(grid, sp$mu[s, i], sp$sd[s, i])))
  })
  total <- dens |>
    dplyr::group_by(biomarker, x) |>
    dplyr::summarise(density = sum(density), .groups = "drop")

  obs_long <- tibble::as_tibble(X) |>
    setNames(fit$resp_disp) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(),
                        names_to = "biomarker", values_to = "value")

  ggplot() +
    geom_histogram(data = obs_long, aes(value, after_stat(density)),
                   bins = 60, fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
    geom_line(data = dens, aes(x, density, colour = state), linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_line(data = total, aes(x, density), linetype = "dashed",
              colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ biomarker, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Raw state") +
    labs(title = title %||% paste0("State-dependent distributions — ", fit$tag),
         subtitle = subtitle %||%
           "Model scale (z-scored, log1p where flagged). Solid: state density x Pr(state). Dashed: mixture.",
         x = NULL, y = "Density") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

# ---- occupancy summary (raw states) ---------------------------------------
occupancy_summary <- function(fit) {
  vit <- fit$hmm$viterbi()
  d   <- tibble::tibble(ID = fit$data$ID, state = vit)
  per <- d |>
    dplyr::group_by(ID) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n_states = dplyr::n_distinct(state), .groups = "drop")
  tibble::tibble(
    model = fit$tag,
    K = fit$K,
    stayers  = sum(per$n_states == 1),
    switchers = sum(per$n_states > 1),
    pct_stayers = round(100 * mean(per$n_states == 1), 1),
    smallest_state_pct =
      round(100 * min(prop.table(table(factor(vit, levels = seq_len(fit$K))))), 1),
    mean_diag_tpm = round(mean(diag(fit$hmm$par()$tpm[, , 1])), 4)
  )
}
```

# 3A. STAGE 1 — Response set: does the inflammatory axis separate states?

The response set is fixed **before** the number of states. The order matters:
$K$ answers "how many regimes does this observation vector resolve", and that
question is only well posed once the observation vector is fixed. Both models
below are fitted at the same $K =$ `r K_AXIS_TEST` on the same cohort, so the
comparison isolates the effect of the response set.

Hypothesis under test: the inflammatory axis (`r AXIS_STEMS[[AXIS_UNDER_TEST]]`)
does not separate the latent states, i.e. its state-dependent marginals
overlap across all state pairs, so it consumes emission parameters without
contributing to the partition.

```{r stage1-config}
# Decision rule, fixed before looking at the fits: drop the axis whose mean
# pairwise overlapping coefficient is the largest AND exceeds this threshold.
OVL_DROP_THRESHOLD <- 0.75
```

## 3A.1 Fit: four axes at K = `r K_AXIS_TEST`

```{r stage1-fit-4axis, cache=TRUE}
fit_4axis <- fit_hmm(data_spec,
                     data_spec$RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE,
                     K = K_AXIS_TEST,
                     tag = "4axes_K4")
```

## 3A.2 Fit: three axes at K = `r K_AXIS_TEST`, same cohort

```{r stage1-fit-3axis, cache=TRUE}
fit_3axis_spec <- fit_hmm(data_spec,
                          data_spec$RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[AXIS_FINAL],
                          K = K_AXIS_TEST,
                          tag = "3axes_K4")
```

## 3A.4 Overlap and separation of the state-dependent marginals

```{r stage1-overlap, fig.height=4.5}

  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(mean_overlap))
save_tab(ovl_tbl, "tab01_stage1_overlap_by_axis",
         caption = paste0("Four-axis model (K = ", K_AXIS_TEST,
                          "): pairwise overlapping coefficient and standardised ",
                          "separation of the state-dependent marginals, by axis. ",
                          "Overlap 1 = the states are indistinguishable along ",
                          "that axis."))

ovl_pairs <- overlap_pairs(fit_4axis) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pair = paste(state_a, state_b, sep = " vs "))

p_ovl <- ggplot(ovl_pairs, aes(pair, biomarker, fill = ovl)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", ovl)), size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#C5000BFF", limits = c(0, 1),
                      name = "Overlapping\ncoefficient") +
  labs(title = paste0("Pairwise overlap of state-dependent marginals (K = ",
                      K_AXIS_TEST, ", four axes)"),

p_ovl

p_ovl_bar <- ggplot(ovl_tbl, aes(reorder(biomarker, mean_overlap), mean_overlap)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#004586FF", width = 0.6) +

  coord_flip(ylim = c(0, 1)) +

       subtitle = paste0("Dashed line: pre-specified drop threshold = ",
                         OVL_DROP_THRESHOLD),
       x = NULL, y = "Mean overlapping coefficient")
p_ovl_bar
save_fig(p_ovl_bar, "fig05_stage1_mean_overlap_by_axis", width = 8, height = 4)
```

## 3A.5 Cost of the fourth axis

```{r stage1-comparison}

                               fit_metrics(fit_3axis_spec))
save_tab(stage1_tbl, "tab02_stage1_model_comparison",
         caption = paste0("Response-set comparison at K = ", K_AXIS_TEST,
                          " on the ", data_spec$label, " cohort. ",
                          "AIC/BIC/ICL are NOT comparable across response sets ",

    "\nso their likelihoods are not on a common scale. The comparison that",
```

## 3A.6 Verdict

```{r stage1-verdict}
worst <- ovl_tbl$biomarker[1]
worst_ovl <- ovl_tbl$mean_overlap[1]
target <- unname(data_spec$RESPONSE_VARS[[AXIS_UNDER_TEST]])

cat("Axis with the largest mean overlap : ", worst,
    " (", round(worst_ovl, 3), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("Axis under test (", AXIS_UNDER_TEST, ")        : ", target, "\n", sep = "")

reproduced <- identical(worst, target) && worst_ovl > OVL_DROP_THRESHOLD
if (reproduced) {
  cat("\nDECISION RULE SATISFIED: the inflammatory axis both has the largest\n",
      "mean pairwise overlap and exceeds the pre-specified threshold of ",
      OVL_DROP_THRESHOLD, ". It is dropped from the response set.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("\n*** DECISION RULE NOT SATISFIED ***\n",
      "The pre-specified rule does not select the inflammatory axis on this\n",
      "run. Do not write the chapter claim as it stands: either the threshold\n",
      "or the argument has to change. The response set below still follows\n",
      "AXIS_FINAL, so the rest of the notebook is runnable, but this result\n",
      "must be reconciled before drafting Section 3.3 of the thesis.\n", sep = "")
}

RESPONSE_AXES_FINAL <- AXIS_FINAL
cat("\nResponse set fixed for everything downstream: ",
    paste(unname(data_spec$RESPONSE_VARS[RESPONSE_AXES_FINAL]), collapse = ", "),
    "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r stage1-cleanup}
# Requirement: discarded candidates are not carried forward. Only the
# summary tables survive Stage 1.
stage1_metrics <- stage1_tbl
stage1_overlap <- ovl_tbl
rm(fit_4axis, fit_3axis_spec, p_dens4, p_dens3)
invisible(gc())
```

---

# 3B. STAGE 2 — Number of latent states

With the response set fixed, $K$ is selected by fitting the candidate models
and weighing the evidence, following the pragmatic protocol of Chapter 2:
fit every candidate in an a-priori plausible range, inspect the fitted
state-dependent distributions, check the decoded occupancy, and read the
information criteria as one input among several rather than as a decision
rule. The range is restricted to `r paste(K_GRID, collapse = ", ")`: below 3
the model cannot represent three clinical axes, and above 5 the fits are
expensive and, in this application, uninterpretable.

```{r stage2-config}
# Set to 3, 4 or 5 to record the final decision explicitly. When NULL, the
# notebook falls back to the BIC-minimising candidate among those that pass
# the interpretability guard below, and says so.
K_FINAL_OVERRIDE <- 4

# Interpretability guard: every state must be occupied by at least this
# share of patient-days in the Viterbi decoding.
MIN_STATE_SHARE_PCT <- 5
```

```{r stage2-cohort}
data_K <- pick_cohort(K_SELECTION_COHORT)
resp_K <- data_K$RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[intersect(RESPONSE_AXES_FINAL,
                                              names(data_K$RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE))]
cat("K selection on cohort: ", data_K$label,
    " (", data_K$n_patients, " patients, ", data_K$n_rows, " patient-days)\n",
    sep = "")
cat("Response set        : ",
    paste(unname(data_K$safe_to_display[unname(resp_K)]), collapse = ", "),
    "\n", sep = "")
```

## 3B.1 Fits

```{r stage2-fits, cache=TRUE}
fits_K <- lapply(K_GRID, function(k)
  fit_hmm(data_K, resp_K, K = k, tag = paste0("3axes_K", k), verbose = TRUE))
names(fits_K) <- paste0("K", K_GRID)
```

## 3B.2 Information criteria

```{r stage2-criteria, fig.height=4.5}
crit_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(fits_K, fit_metrics)
save_tab(crit_tbl, "tab03_stage2_information_criteria",
         caption = paste0("Candidate models on the fixed response set, cohort: ",
                          data_K$label,
                          ". npar excludes the initial distribution, which is ",
                          "constrained to the stationary distribution of Gamma."))

crit_long <- crit_tbl |>
  dplyr::select(K, AIC, BIC, ICL) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-K, names_to = "criterion", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(value))

p_crit <- ggplot(crit_long, aes(factor(K), value, group = criterion,
                                colour = criterion)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ criterion, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1", guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Information criteria against the number of states",
       subtitle = paste0("Cohort: ", data_K$label,
                         "; smaller is better. Criteria are guidance, not a ",
                         "decision rule (Chapter 2)."),
       x = "Number of latent states K", y = NULL)
p_crit
save_fig(p_crit, "fig06_stage2_information_criteria", width = 10, height = 4)
```

## 3B.3 Fitted state-dependent distributions per K

```{r stage2-densities, fig.height=12}
dens_panels <- lapply(names(fits_K), function(nm)
  plot_state_densities(fits_K[[nm]],
                       title = paste0("K = ", fits_K[[nm]]$K),
                       subtitle = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "right"))
p_dens_K <- patchwork::wrap_plots(dens_panels, ncol = 1) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(

p_dens_K
```

## 3B.4 Separation and occupancy per K

```{r stage2-separation, fig.height=4.5}

save_tab(sep_tbl, "tab04_stage2_overlap_by_K",
         caption = "Overlap and separation of the state-dependent marginals, by candidate K.")

occ_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(fits_K, occupancy_summary)
save_tab(occ_tbl, "tab05_stage2_occupancy_by_K",
         caption = paste0("Decoded occupancy by candidate K. `smallest_state_pct` ",
                          "is the share of patient-days assigned to the least ",
                          "occupied state; states below ", MIN_STATE_SHARE_PCT,
                          "% are treated as not interpretable."))

p_sep <- ggplot(sep_tbl, aes(factor(model), mean_overlap, fill = biomarker)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Mean pairwise overlap of state-dependent marginals, by K",
       subtitle = "Lower is better: the states are more clearly separated along that axis",
       x = NULL, y = "Mean overlapping coefficient") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
p_sep
save_fig(p_sep, "fig08_stage2_overlap_by_K", width = 9, height = 4.5)
```

## 3B.5 Selection

```{r stage2-verdict}
guard <- occ_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(passes = smallest_state_pct >= MIN_STATE_SHARE_PCT) |>
  dplyr::select(model, K, smallest_state_pct, passes)
print(guard)

eligible <- guard$K[guard$passes]
bic_pick <- crit_tbl$K[which.min(crit_tbl$BIC)]
bic_pick_eligible <- if (length(eligible) > 0) {
  crit_tbl$K[crit_tbl$K %in% eligible][which.min(crit_tbl$BIC[crit_tbl$K %in% eligible])]
} else {
  NA_integer_
}

cat("\nBIC-minimising K (all candidates)          : ", bic_pick, "\n", sep = "")
cat("BIC-minimising K (passing occupancy guard) : ", bic_pick_eligible, "\n", sep = "")

if (!is.null(K_FINAL_OVERRIDE)) {
  K_FINAL <- K_FINAL_OVERRIDE
  cat("\nK fixed by explicit decision: K = ", K_FINAL, ".\n", sep = "")
  if (!identical(as.integer(K_FINAL), as.integer(bic_pick)))
    cat("This differs from the BIC-minimising candidate (K = ", bic_pick,
        "). The thesis must state the reason (interpretability of the ",
        "additional state), per Remark 'Status of the selected order' in ",
        "Chapter 2.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  K_FINAL <- bic_pick_eligible
  cat("\nNo explicit decision recorded; falling back to the BIC-minimising ",
      "candidate that passes the occupancy guard: K = ", K_FINAL, ".\n", sep = "")
}
stopifnot(K_FINAL %in% K_GRID)
```

```{r stage2-cleanup}
# Requirement: no discarded candidate survives this point.
stage2_criteria  <- crit_tbl
stage2_overlap   <- sep_tbl
stage2_occupancy <- occ_tbl
rm(fits_K, dens_panels, p_dens_K)
invisible(gc())
cat("Candidate models discarded. From here on the notebook uses one model:\n")
cat("  response set : ",
    paste(unname(data_spec$RESPONSE_VARS[RESPONSE_AXES_FINAL]), collapse = ", "),
    "\n  K            : ", K_FINAL,
    "\n  cohort       : ", pick_cohort(FINAL_COHORT)$label, "\n", sep = "")
```

# 4. Final model specification

Everything below applies to a single model: the response set fixed in
Section 3A and the state count fixed in Section 3B, refitted from scratch on
the cohort selected by `FINAL_COHORT`. No candidate from the two selection
stages is reused.

```{r final-promote}
data_final <- pick_cohort(FINAL_COHORT)

resp_final_axes <- intersect(RESPONSE_AXES_FINAL,
                             names(data_final$RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE))
resp_final_safe <- unname(data_final$RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[resp_final_axes])

# Promote this cohort's data frame and back-transform helpers to the global
# names that Sections 6-12 (unchanged from the previous notebook) read.
use_dataset(data_final, resp_final_safe)

N_STATES <- as.integer(K_FINAL)
DATA_PATH               <- data_final$data_path
BM_LOG1P_DECISIONS_PATH <- if (identical(FINAL_COHORT, "spec"))
  SPEC_DECISIONS_PATH else FULL_DECISIONS_PATH

cat("Final model\n")
cat("  cohort        : ", data_final$label, " (", data_final$n_patients,
    " patients, ", data_final$n_rows, " patient-days)\n", sep = "")
cat("  response set  : ", paste(RESPONSE_VARS, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
cat("  latent states : ", N_STATES, "\n", sep = "")
cat("  covariates    : ", if (has_covariates)
      paste(OBS_COVARIATES, collapse = ", ") else "none", "\n", sep = "")
cat("  hold-out      : none (TEST_FRAC = 0)\n")
```

## 4.1 Parameter count rationale

```{r param-count-rationale, echo=FALSE}
p      <- length(RESPONSE_VARS)
n_cov  <- p * (p - 1) / 2
p_all  <- length(bio_cols)
n_cov_all <- p_all * (p_all - 1) / 2
n_extra_per_state <- length(OBS_COVARIATES)

indep_sel  <- p * 2 * N_STATES
mvn_sel    <- (p + p + n_cov) * N_STATES
indep_all  <- p_all * 2 * N_STATES
mvn_all    <- (p_all + p_all + n_cov_all) * N_STATES
extra_obs  <- if (has_covariates) p * N_STATES * n_extra_per_state else 0

param_tbl <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    paste0(p, " independent normals — selected biomarkers",
           if (!IS_a_MVN) " **(this model)**" else ""),
    paste0(p, "-dim full MVN — selected biomarkers",
           if (IS_a_MVN) " **(this model)**" else ""),
    paste0(p_all, " independent normals — all available biomarkers"),
    paste0(p_all, "-dim full MVN — all available biomarkers")
  ),
  Formula = c(
    paste0(p, " vars × 2 params × ", N_STATES, " states"),
    paste0("(", p, " means + ", p, " sds + ", n_cov, " corrs) × ", N_STATES, " states"),
    paste0(p_all, " vars × 2 params × ", N_STATES, " states"),
    paste0("(", p_all, " means + ", p_all, " sds + ", n_cov_all, " corrs) × ", N_STATES, " states")
  ),
  `Obs. parameters (no covariates)` = c(indep_sel, mvn_sel, indep_all, mvn_all),
  check.names = FALSE
)

cap <- paste0("Observation parameter counts for ", N_STATES,
              " states and ", p, " selected biomarkers (", p_all,
              " total available).")
if (has_covariates) {
  cap <- paste0(cap, " The configured covariates (",
                paste(OBS_COVARIATES, collapse = ", "),
                ") add ", extra_obs,
                " extra mean-effect coefficients to the selected model.")
}
knitr::kable(param_tbl, align = c("l", "l", "r"), caption = cap)
```


---

# 5. Final model fitting

The likelihood of a hidden Markov model is generally multimodal, and a single
optimisation started from one $k$-means partition reaches a local maximum with
no guarantee that it is the global one. The final model is therefore obtained
by a best-of-$R$ multi-start procedure: the fit is repeated from $R$ perturbed
starting points, and the solution attaining the highest maximised
log-likelihood is retained. Every downstream section uses that solution.

```{r final-fit, cache=TRUE}
N_STARTS  <- 25     # perturbed starts, in addition to the unperturbed one
JITTER_SD <- 0.5    # displacement of the k-means centres, in units of the
                    # marginal sd; sds are scaled by a lognormal factor

fit_one <- function(r) {
  tryCatch(
    fit_hmm(data_final, resp_final_safe, K = N_STATES,
            seed = if (r == 0) SEED else SEED + 7919 * r,
            jitter_sd = if (r == 0) 0 else JITTER_SD,
            tag = if (r == 0) "start_0_kmeans" else paste0("start_", r),
            verbose = FALSE),
    error = function(e) { warning("start ", r, " failed: ",
                                  conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
}

starts <- lapply(0:N_STARTS, fit_one)
ok     <- !vapply(starts, is.null, logical(1))
lls    <- vapply(starts, function(f) if (is.null(f)) NA_real_ else fit_loglik(f),
                 numeric(1))

best_i <- which.max(lls)
final    <- starts[[best_i]]
hmm      <- final$hmm
hmm_data <- final$data

start_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  start       = c("0 (k-means, unperturbed)", paste0(1:N_STARTS, " (perturbed)")),
  logLik      = lls,
  convergence = vapply(starts, function(f)
                  if (is.null(f)) NA_integer_ else as.integer(f$out$convergence),
                  integer(1)),
  iterations  = vapply(starts, function(f)
                  if (is.null(f)) NA_integer_ else as.integer(f$out$iterations),
                  integer(1))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(gap_to_best = round(max(logLik, na.rm = TRUE) - logLik, 4),
                retained    = dplyr::row_number() == best_i)

save_tab(start_tbl, "tab06_final_multistart", digits = 4,
         caption = paste0("Maximised log-likelihood from ", N_STARTS + 1,
                          " starting points (one k-means partition and ",
                          N_STARTS, " perturbations of it). The retained model ",
                          "is the row with gap_to_best = 0."))

# Distinct local maxima actually visited, to the nearest 0.01 nats.
modes <- as.data.frame(table(round(lls[ok], 2)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  setNames(c("logLik", "n_starts")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(as.numeric(logLik)))
save_tab(modes, "tab06b_final_local_maxima", digits = 4,
         caption = paste0("Distinct local maxima visited by the ", sum(ok),
                          " successful starts, and how many starts reached each."))

cat("\n-- Retained model --\n")
cat("start index          : ", best_i - 1, "\n", sep = "")
cat("maximised logLik     : ", format(lls[best_i], digits = 12), "\n", sep = "")
cat("starts reaching it   : ", sum(abs(lls - lls[best_i]) < 1e-3, na.rm = TRUE),
    " of ", sum(ok), "\n", sep = "")
cat("distinct local maxima: ", nrow(modes), "\n", sep = "")
cat("gap to the k-means solution: ",
    round(lls[best_i] - lls[1], 4), " log-likelihood units\n", sep = "")

out <- hmm$out()
cat("\nConvergence code:", out$convergence, "\n")
cat("Message:", out$message, "\n")
cat("Final negative log-likelihood:", format(out$objective, digits = 12), "\n")
cat("Iterations used:", out$iterations, "\n")

cat("\n-- Estimated parameters --\n")
hmm
```

## 5.1 Starting values of the retained fit

```{r final-startvals}
cat("Default initial transition matrix (hmmTMB):\n")
print(round(MarkovChain$new(data = hmm_data, n_states = N_STATES,
                            initial_state = "stationary")$tpm()[, , 1], 4))

cat("\nStandardisation constants of the estimation scale:\n")
print(as.data.frame(zscore_params), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 5.2 Clinical state labels — final model only

Raw state indices come from the $k$-means initialisation and carry no
clinical meaning. Labels are assigned here, from the estimated state means
in clinical units, and only to this model.

The previous label set contained one state called *Weak*, which conflated
two distinct profiles, and one called *Epatic*, an Italianism. Both are
retired. The label set is now **Stable / Anaemic / Hepatic / Renal**, assigned
by the following deterministic rule (K = 4):

1. **Renal** — the state with the highest mean creatinine.
2. **Hepatic** — among the remaining states, the highest mean ALT.
3. **Anaemic** — among the remaining states, the lowest mean haemoglobin.
4. **Stable** — the state left over.

```{r final-state-labels}
op_final <- hmm$par()$obspar[, , 1]                 # raw state order
mu_model <- sapply(seq_along(resp_final_safe), function(i) op_final[paste0("z.mu", i), ])
mu_model <- matrix(mu_model, nrow = N_STATES)
colnames(mu_model) <- resp_final_safe

mu_clin <- mu_model
for (i in seq_along(resp_final_safe))
  mu_clin[, i] <- to_clinical(mu_model[, i], resp_final_safe[i])
colnames(mu_clin) <- display_vec(resp_final_safe)

cat("Estimated state means in clinical units (RAW state order):\n")
print(round(as.data.frame(mu_clin), 3))

axis_col <- function(axis) {
  sfe <- data_final$RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[[axis]]
  match(sfe, resp_final_safe)
}

if (!is.null(STATE_LABELS_MAP_OVERRIDE)) {
  STATE_LABELS_MAP    <- STATE_LABELS_MAP_OVERRIDE
  STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER <- STATE_LABEL_ORDER
  cat("\nUsing the manual label override from Section 0.\n")

} else if (N_STATES == 4L && all(c("renal", "hepatic", "haematological")
                                 %in% resp_final_axes)) {
  remaining <- seq_len(N_STATES)
  i_renal   <- remaining[which.max(mu_clin[remaining, axis_col("renal")])]
  remaining <- setdiff(remaining, i_renal)
  i_hep     <- remaining[which.max(mu_clin[remaining, axis_col("hepatic")])]
  remaining <- setdiff(remaining, i_hep)
  i_anaem   <- remaining[which.min(mu_clin[remaining, axis_col("haematological")])]
  i_stable  <- setdiff(remaining, i_anaem)

  lab <- character(N_STATES)
  lab[i_renal]  <- "Renal state"
  lab[i_hep]    <- "Hepatic state"
  lab[i_anaem]  <- "Anaemic state"
  lab[i_stable] <- "Stable state"

  STATE_LABELS_MAP    <- as.list(setNames(lab, as.character(seq_len(N_STATES))))
  STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER <- STATE_LABEL_ORDER
  cat("\nAutomatic clinical labelling (raw index -> label):\n")
  print(unlist(STATE_LABELS_MAP))

} else {
  STATE_LABELS_MAP    <- NULL
  STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER <- NULL
  warning("Automatic labelling is defined for K = 4 with the renal/hepatic/",
          "haematological axes present. K = ", N_STATES,
          " -> falling back to raw state numbering. Set ",
          "STATE_LABELS_MAP_OVERRIDE in Section 0 to label these states.")
}
```

```{r final-state-remap}
USE_CUSTOM_STATE_LABELS <-
  !is.null(STATE_LABELS_MAP) && !is.null(STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER)

if (USE_CUSTOM_STATE_LABELS) {
  if (length(STATE_LABELS_MAP) != N_STATES)
    stop("STATE_LABELS_MAP must have length ", N_STATES, ".")
  if (!setequal(names(STATE_LABELS_MAP), as.character(seq_len(N_STATES))))
    stop("STATE_LABELS_MAP names must be \"1\"..\"", N_STATES, "\".")
  if (!setequal(STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER, unlist(STATE_LABELS_MAP)))
    stop("STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER labels must match STATE_LABELS_MAP values.")

  state_remap <- vapply(
    seq_len(N_STATES),
    function(i) match(STATE_LABELS_MAP[[as.character(i)]], STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER),
    integer(1))
  state_levels <- STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER

  state_palette_vec <-
    if (!is.null(STATE_PALETTE_CUSTOM) &&
        length(STATE_PALETTE_CUSTOM) == N_STATES) STATE_PALETTE_CUSTOM
    else unname(pal[seq_len(N_STATES)])
} else {
  state_remap       <- seq_len(N_STATES)
  state_levels      <- paste0("State ", seq_len(N_STATES))
  state_palette_vec <- unname(pal[seq_len(N_STATES)])
}

state_remap_inv <- order(state_remap)
state_colours   <- setNames(state_palette_vec, state_levels)
relabel_state_token <- function(raw_idx) state_levels[state_remap[raw_idx]]

cat("State remap (raw -> new):\n"); print(setNames(state_remap, paste0("raw_", seq_len(N_STATES))))
cat("\nState levels (display order):\n"); print(state_levels)
```

### Verification of the labelling

```{r final-label-check}
label_check <- as.data.frame(mu_clin)
label_check$raw_state <- seq_len(N_STATES)
label_check$label     <- state_levels[state_remap]
label_check <- label_check |>
  dplyr::relocate(raw_state, label) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(label, state_levels))
save_tab(label_check, "tab07_final_state_labels",
         caption = paste0("Final model: estimated state means in clinical units ",
                          "and the label assigned to each state. Check every row ",
                          "before the labels are used in the thesis."))
```

# 6. State Decoding

## 6.1 Viterbi sequence (global decoding)

Raw Viterbi indices (1..N from hmmTMB) are reordered to the clinical
numbering via `state_remap`, then assigned the canonical labels in
`state_levels`. The resulting factor uses the new ordering everywhere.

```{r viterbi}
viterbi_raw <- hmm$viterbi()
viterbi_new <- state_remap[viterbi_raw]
hmm_data$state <- factor(state_levels[viterbi_new], levels = state_levels)

cat("State distribution across all patient-days (Viterbi):\n")
print(table(hmm_data$state))
cat("\nAs proportions:\n")
print(round(prop.table(table(hmm_data$state)), 3))
```

## 6.2 State probabilities (local decoding)

```{r state-probs}
sp_mat <- hmm$state_probs()                                       # raw order
# Reorder columns: column i in the new order is column state_remap_inv[i] raw
sp_mat <- sp_mat[, state_remap_inv, drop = FALSE]
colnames(sp_mat) <- paste0("Pr_state", 1:N_STATES)
hmm_data <- bind_cols(hmm_data, as_tibble(sp_mat))
```

## 6.3 Trajectory plot — first 9 patients

```{r trajectory-plot, fig.height=10}
first_ids <- levels(hmm_data$ID)[1:9]

traj_data <- hmm_data |>
  filter(ID %in% first_ids) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE),
               names_to = "biomarker_safe", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(biomarker_safe) |>
  mutate(value_clin = mapply(to_clinical, value, biomarker_safe)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(biomarker_lbl = factor(
    vapply(biomarker_safe, axis_label, character(1)),
    levels = vapply(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE, axis_label, character(1))
  ))

traj_data |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value_clin, colour = state, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_grid(biomarker_lbl ~ ID, scales = "free_y") +

    subtitle = global_scale_subtitle(),

        strip.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
```

# 7. Model Visualisation

## 7.1 State-dependent distributions (workflow-style)

Layout:

- **Covariate-free model.** Each biomarker gets one density panel
  (model scale) plus an optional clinical-scale companion if the
  biomarker is back-transformed (log1p) or z-scored. Densities are
  stationary, since none of the parameters depend on time.

- **Covariate-augmented model.** Each (biomarker, covariate) pair gets
  one density panel per scale, with three sub-panels (`facet_wrap`)
  showing the density at the **25th, 50th, 75th percentile** of that
  covariate while every *other* covariate is held at its median (numeric)
  or modal level (factor). This visualises how the state-conditional
  distributions move when the covariate varies, the standard hmmTMB
  workflow trick for inspecting Markov-switching GLM emissions.

```{r plot-dist, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}
# ── State setup ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Recover the new (clinical) state index per row from the renumbered factor.
viterbi_states_new <- as.integer(hmm_data$state)
state_weights_new  <- as.numeric(
  prop.table(table(factor(viterbi_states_new, levels = seq_len(N_STATES))))
)

# ── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Build a one-row "baseline" data frame with every covariate fixed at its
# representative value: median (numeric) or modal level (factor). Used as
# the starting point for the per-quantile grids below. Scalars are
# stripped of any names attribute (mean()/median() may inherit one from
# the column and trip up hmm$predict() downstream — same gotcha as
# Section 7.5).
baseline_covariate_row <- function(data = hmm_data) {
  if (!has_covariates) return(NULL)
  out <- lapply(OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE, function(c) {
    v <- data[[c]]
    if (is.numeric(v)) {
      unname(as.numeric(median(v, na.rm = TRUE)))
    } else {
      tab <- sort(table(v), decreasing = TRUE)
      mode_lvl <- names(tab)[1]
      if (is.factor(v)) factor(mode_lvl, levels = levels(v)) else mode_lvl
    }
  })
  names(out) <- OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE
  as.data.frame(out, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# For a focus covariate, build a 3-row newdata that varies it on Q25/Q50/Q75
# while every other covariate stays at its baseline value. For categorical
# focus covariates we use the three most frequent levels (or all of them
# if there are <= 3).
build_focus_newdata <- function(focus_cov_safe, data = hmm_data) {
  base <- baseline_covariate_row(data)
  v <- data[[focus_cov_safe]]
  if (is.numeric(v)) {
    qs <- quantile(v, probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE,
               names = FALSE, type = 7)
    labs <- c("Q05", "Q50", "Q95")
    vals <- unname(as.numeric(qs))
  } else {
    tab <- sort(table(v), decreasing = TRUE)
    n_show <- min(3L, length(tab))
    vals <- names(tab)[seq_len(n_show)]
    labs <- vals
    if (is.factor(v)) vals <- factor(vals, levels = levels(v))
  }
  newdata <- base[rep(1, length(vals)), , drop = FALSE]
  newdata[[focus_cov_safe]] <- vals
  rownames(newdata) <- NULL
  list(newdata = newdata, labs = labs, vals = vals)
}

# Pull (mu, sd) per state at a SINGLE time slice of obspar.
# `obs_par_slice` is the (par x state) matrix already permuted to CLINICAL
# state order. Returns mu / sd vectors of length N_STATES in clinical
# ordering.
get_state_mu_sd_from_slice <- function(b_idx, biomarker_safe, obs_par_slice) {
  if (IS_a_MVN) {
    mu_row <- paste0("z.mu", b_idx); sd_row <- paste0("z.sd", b_idx)
  } else {
    mu_row <- paste0(biomarker_safe, ".mean")
    sd_row <- paste0(biomarker_safe, ".sd")
  }
  list(mu = obs_par_slice[mu_row, ],
       sd = obs_par_slice[sd_row, ])
}

# Build the long-format density data frame for ONE (biomarker, scale,
# covariate-slice) panel. obs_par_slice is already in CLINICAL state order.
build_density_long <- function(b_idx, biomarker_safe, obs_par_slice,
                               grid_model, scale = c("model", "clinical")) {
  scale <- match.arg(scale)
  ms <- get_state_mu_sd_from_slice(b_idx, biomarker_safe, obs_par_slice)

  dens_state <- lapply(seq_len(N_STATES), function(s) {
    data.frame(
      x_model = grid_model,
      density = state_weights_new[s] * dnorm(grid_model, ms$mu[s], ms$sd[s]),
      state   = factor(state_levels[s], levels = state_levels)
    )
  }) |> do.call(rbind, args = _)

  if (scale == "model") {
    dens_state$x_plot <- dens_state$x_model
  } else {
    dens_state$x_plot <- to_clinical(dens_state$x_model, biomarker_safe)
    # Jacobians to preserve area = 1 under the back-transform.
    if (isTRUE(needs_expm1[[biomarker_safe]])) {
      dens_state$density <- dens_state$density / (1 + dens_state$x_plot)
    }
    if (APPLY_ZSCORE) {
      sd0 <- zscore_params$sd[zscore_params$biomarker == biomarker_safe]
      dens_state$density <- dens_state$density / sd0
    }
  }

  # Total mixture density across states, per grid point.
  dens_total <- dens_state |>
    group_by(x_plot) |>
    summarise(density = sum(density), .groups = "drop")

  list(state = dens_state, total = dens_total)
}

# Render ONE panel (= one biomarker, one scale, optionally faceted by
# covariate slices). Returns a ggplot object.
render_panel <- function(b_idx, biomarker_safe, scale,
                         slices_df = NULL) {
  # slices_df: a long data.frame with columns
  #   x_plot, density, state, slice_label
  # plus a separate "total" df with x_plot/density/slice_label.
  # If NULL we are in the covariate-free case and slices_df is built from
  # a single obs_par_t1 slice (no facets).

  obs_vals_model <- hmm_data[[biomarker_safe]]
  rng <- range(obs_vals_model, na.rm = TRUE)
  grid_model <- seq(rng[1] - 0.1 * diff(rng),
                    rng[2] + 0.1 * diff(rng),
                    length.out = 400)

  if (is.null(slices_df)) {
    obs_par_clinical <- hmm$par()$obspar[, , 1][, state_remap_inv, drop = FALSE]
    dens <- build_density_long(b_idx, biomarker_safe, obs_par_clinical,
                               grid_model, scale = scale)
    dens$state$slice_label <- "(no covariate)"
    dens$total$slice_label <- "(no covariate)"
    slices_df <- list(state = dens$state, total = dens$total)
  }

  x_obs <- if (scale == "model") obs_vals_model
           else to_clinical(obs_vals_model, biomarker_safe)

  x_lab    <- if (scale == "model") paste0(display(biomarker_safe), " (model scale)")
              else axis_label(biomarker_safe)
  subtitle <- if (scale == "clinical") "Back-transformed (Jacobian applied)" else NULL

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_histogram(data = data.frame(x = x_obs),
                   aes(x = x, y = after_stat(density)),
                   bins = 40, fill = "grey80", colour = "white", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_line(data = slices_df$state,
              aes(x = x_plot, y = density, colour = state),
              linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_line(data = slices_df$total,
              aes(x = x_plot, y = density),
              colour = "grey30", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = state_colours, name = NULL) +
    labs(title = display(biomarker_safe), subtitle = subtitle,
         x = x_lab, y = "Density") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8))

  # Facet only when we have more than one slice.
  if (length(unique(slices_df$state$slice_label)) > 1L) {
    p <- p + facet_wrap(~ slice_label, scales = "fixed")
  }

  # Clinical reference interval, drawn on whichever scale the panel uses:
  # native units on the clinical axis, forwarded through to_model() (log1p
  # where flagged + z-score) on the model axis.
  ri <- ref_by_safe(biomarker_safe)
  if (!is.null(ri)) {
    bounds <- c(ri$lln, ri$uln)
    if (scale == "model") bounds <- to_model(bounds, biomarker_safe)
    p <- p +
      annotate("rect", xmin = bounds[1], xmax = bounds[2],
               ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.06, fill = "forestgreen") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = bounds,
                 linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.5)
  }
  p
}

# ── Drivers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!has_covariates) {
  # ---- Covariate-free path (legacy behaviour) ----
  model_panels <- lapply(seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE), function(i)
    render_panel(i, RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i], "model", slices_df = NULL))
  print(
    wrap_plots(model_panels, ncol = min(length(model_panels), 2)) +
      plot_annotation(
        title    = "State-dependent distributions — model scale",
        subtitle = "Solid: state-specific normal density × Pr(state). Dashed grey: total mixture."
      )
  )

  needs_clinical <- vapply(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE,
    function(b) isTRUE(needs_expm1[[b]]) || APPLY_ZSCORE,
    logical(1))
  if (any(needs_clinical)) {
    clin_idx <- which(needs_clinical)
    clinical_panels <- lapply(clin_idx, function(i)
      render_panel(i, RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i], "clinical", slices_df = NULL))
    print(
      wrap_plots(clinical_panels, ncol = min(length(clinical_panels), 2)) +
        plot_annotation(
          title    = "State-dependent distributions — clinical scale (back-transformed)",
          subtitle = "Same densities with the log1p / z-score Jacobian applied to preserve area = 1."
        )
    )
  }

} else {
  # ---- Covariate-augmented path: one plot per (covariate, biomarker, scale)
  # with three facets (Q25/Q50/Q75 of the focus covariate). ----
  for (focus_cov in OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE) {
    focus_disp <- display(focus_cov)
    cat("\n\n### Effects of `", focus_disp, "` on state distributions\n\n",
        sep = "")

    fb <- build_focus_newdata(focus_cov)
    newdata <- fb$newdata
    slice_labels <- paste0(focus_disp, " = ",
                           if (is.numeric(fb$vals)) sprintf("%.3g", fb$vals)
                           else as.character(fb$vals),
                           " (", fb$labs, ")")

    # hmm$predict("obspar", newdata = ...) returns a [par, state, time] array
    # with `state` in RAW order. Permute to clinical ordering once per slice.
    pred <- hmm$predict("obspar", newdata = newdata, n_post = 0)
    # pred dim is [n_par, N_STATES, nrow(newdata)]; permute middle dim.
    pred_clinical <- pred[, state_remap_inv, , drop = FALSE]

    for (i in seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)) {
      bsafe <- RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]

      obs_vals_model <- hmm_data[[bsafe]]
      rng <- range(obs_vals_model, na.rm = TRUE)
      grid_model <- seq(rng[1] - 0.1 * diff(rng),
                        rng[2] + 0.1 * diff(rng),
                        length.out = 400)

      for (scale in c("model", "clinical")) {
        # Skip clinical if no back-transform is in play for this biomarker.
        if (scale == "clinical" &&
            !(isTRUE(needs_expm1[[bsafe]]) || APPLY_ZSCORE)) next

        # Build the long data frame across all 3 slices.
        per_slice <- lapply(seq_along(slice_labels), function(k) {
          obs_par_slice_k <- pred_clinical[, , k]
          d <- build_density_long(i, bsafe, obs_par_slice_k,
                                  grid_model, scale = scale)
          d$state$slice_label <- slice_labels[k]
          d$total$slice_label <- slice_labels[k]
          d
        })
        slices_df <- list(
          state = do.call(rbind, lapply(per_slice, `[[`, "state")),
          total = do.call(rbind, lapply(per_slice, `[[`, "total"))
        )
        # Lock facet order to match the slice ordering.
        slices_df$state$slice_label <- factor(slices_df$state$slice_label,
                                              levels = slice_labels)
        slices_df$total$slice_label <- factor(slices_df$total$slice_label,
                                              levels = slice_labels)

        p <- render_panel(i, bsafe, scale, slices_df = slices_df) +
          labs(title = paste0(display(bsafe),
                              " — varies with ", focus_disp,
                              if (scale == "clinical") " (clinical scale)"
                              else " (model scale)"))
        print(p)
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## 7.2 Transition probability matrix

```{r tpm-heatmap, fig.height=4}
# tpm has rows/cols in raw state order; permute both to the new order so
# states appear consistently across all plots.
tpm_est_raw <- hmm$par()$tpm[, , 1]
tpm_est     <- tpm_est_raw[state_remap_inv, state_remap_inv, drop = FALSE]
rownames(tpm_est) <- paste0("From ", state_levels)
colnames(tpm_est) <- paste0("To ",   state_levels)

as.data.frame(tpm_est) |>
  rownames_to_column("from") |>
  pivot_longer(-from, names_to = "to", values_to = "prob") |>
  mutate(
    from = factor(from, levels = paste0("From ", state_levels)),
    to   = factor(to,   levels = paste0("To ",   state_levels))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(to, from, fill = prob)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(prob, 3)), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#1a6faf", limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Estimated transition probability matrix",
       x = "To state", y = "From state", fill = "Probability") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
```

## 7.3 MVN state-dependent correlation matrices

```{r mvn-corr-heatmap, fig.height=5, eval=IS_a_MVN}
if(IS_a_MVN){
  n_vars   <- length(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)
  # Permute columns to clinical state order so facet labels match the rest
  # of the notebook.
  obs_pars <- hmm$par()$obspar[, , 1][, state_remap_inv, drop = FALSE]
  
  # hmmTMB stores correlations as "z.corrXY" with X < Y. Use upper.tri to get
  # (i, j) with i < j directly.
  pairs      <- which(upper.tri(matrix(0, n_vars, n_vars)), arr.ind = TRUE)
  corr_names <- paste0("z.corr", pairs[, 1], pairs[, 2])
  
  missing_corr <- setdiff(corr_names, rownames(obs_pars))
  if (length(missing_corr) > 0)
    warning("Some correlation parameters not found in obspar: ",
            paste(missing_corr, collapse = ", "))
  
  corr_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:N_STATES, function(s) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(k) {
      i <- pairs[k, 1]; j <- pairs[k, 2]
      nm <- corr_names[k]
      rho <- if (nm %in% rownames(obs_pars)) obs_pars[nm, s] else NA_real_
      # s is now the NEW state index (columns reordered above)
      data.frame(state = state_levels[s],
                 var_i = RESPONSE_VARS[i],   # display names directly
                 var_j = RESPONSE_VARS[j],
                 rho   = rho)
    }))
  }))
  
  corr_full <- bind_rows(
    corr_df,
    corr_df |> rename(var_i = var_j, var_j = var_i),
    data.frame(
      state = rep(state_levels, each = n_vars),
      var_i = rep(RESPONSE_VARS, N_STATES),
      var_j = rep(RESPONSE_VARS, N_STATES),
      rho   = 1
    )
  )
  
  corr_full$state <- factor(corr_full$state, levels = state_levels)
  corr_full$var_i <- factor(corr_full$var_i, levels = RESPONSE_VARS)
  corr_full$var_j <- factor(corr_full$var_j, levels = rev(RESPONSE_VARS))
  
  ggplot(corr_full, aes(var_i, var_j, fill = rho)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(!is.na(rho), sprintf("%.2f", rho), "")),
              size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~ state, ncol = N_STATES) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#d73027", mid = "white", high = "#1a6faf",
                         midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1),
                         name = "Pearson\ncorrelation") +
    labs(title = "Fitted state-dependent correlation matrices (MVN model)",
         subtitle = "Correlations are scale-free (log1p back-transform does not affect them)",
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 8),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
}
```
