## 7.4 Stationary state distribution

```{r stationary, fig.height=4}
# Solve the stationary equation on the RAW TPM, then permute the resulting
# probability vector to clinical state order.
tpm_m <- hmm$par()$tpm[, , 1]
K     <- nrow(tpm_m)
A     <- t(tpm_m - diag(K))
A     <- rbind(A, rep(1, K))
b_vec <- c(rep(0, K), 1)
pi_stat_raw <- as.numeric(solve(t(A) %*% A, t(A) %*% b_vec))
pi_stat     <- pi_stat_raw[state_remap_inv]
names(pi_stat) <- state_levels

cat("Stationary state probabilities:\n")
print(round(pi_stat, 4))

data.frame(state = factor(names(pi_stat), levels = state_levels),
           prob  = as.numeric(pi_stat)) |>
  ggplot(aes(state, prob, fill = state)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(prob, 3)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_colours) +
  labs(title = "Stationary state distribution",
       x = "State", y = "Probability") +
  ylim(0, max(pi_stat) * 1.15)
```

```{r save-fig-stationary, echo=FALSE}
save_fig(ggplot2::last_plot(), "fig15_final_stationary_distribution",
         width = 7, height = 4.5)
```

## 7.5 Covariate effects on state-specific means

We now allow the state-specific mean of each response biomarker to depend
linearly on the configured covariates. This corresponds to a Markov-switching
generalised linear model — an extension of Markov-switching regression — in
which the state-process $\{S_t\}$ retains its Markov structure but each
emission distribution carries its own intercept-plus-slope mean function:

$$
Y_{t,k}\,|\,\{S_t = j\} \;\sim\; \mathcal{N}\!\bigl(\mu_{j,k},\,\sigma_{j,k}\bigr),
\qquad
\mu_{j,k} \;=\; \beta^{(j,k)}_{0} \;+\; \sum_{\ell=1}^{p}\beta^{(j,k)}_{\ell}\,x_{\ell,t},
$$

for biomarker $k \in \{1,\dots,K\}$, state $j \in \{1,\dots,N\}$, and
covariate vector $\mathbf{x}_t = (x_{1,t},\dots,x_{p,t})^\top$. Here
$\beta^{(j,k)}_{0}$ is the state-and-biomarker-specific intercept and
$\beta^{(j,k)}_{\ell}$ the slope of covariate $\ell$ on the mean of
biomarker $k$ in state $j$. Standard deviations $\sigma_{j,k}$ and
(for MVN models) state-conditional correlations are kept covariate-free
for interpretability. This specification is exactly what we encoded in
Section 4.4 via the nested `formulas` argument to `Observation$new()`.

For each (covariate × response biomarker) pair we visualise the fitted
$\mu_{j,k}$ as a function of that covariate, with observations from each
Viterbi state overlaid for context.

```{r covariate-effects, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5, eval=has_covariates}
# hmm$plot() emits the state factor as "State 1".."State N" in RAW
# order (the order hmmTMB picked at fit time). Override its colour /
# fill scales so each raw state shows the clinical colour and label
# defined by state_remap (Section 1.1). Legend order is also forced
# to the clinical sequence.
raw_state_keys <- paste0("State ", seq_len(N_STATES))
plot_colours   <- setNames(
  state_colours[state_levels[state_remap[seq_len(N_STATES)]]],
  raw_state_keys
)
plot_labels    <- setNames(
  state_levels[state_remap[seq_len(N_STATES)]],
  raw_state_keys
)
legend_breaks  <- raw_state_keys[state_remap_inv]

for (cov_safe in OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE) {
  cov_disp <- display(cov_safe)
  cat("\n\n### Effects of `", cov_disp, "`\n\n", sep = "")

  for (i in seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)) {
    bsafe  <- RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]
    bdisp  <- display(bsafe)
    par_id <- if (IS_a_MVN) paste0("z.mu", i) else paste0(bsafe, ".mean")

    # Overlay observations: hmm_data$state is already in CLINICAL levels
    # (from Section 6.1); remap back to the raw "State r" keys that
    # hmm$plot() uses, so colours line up with the curves.
    obs_df <- data.frame(
      x     = hmm_data[[cov_safe]],
      y     = hmm_data[[bsafe]],
      state = factor(
        raw_state_keys[match(as.character(hmm_data$state),
                             state_levels[state_remap[seq_len(N_STATES)]])],
        levels = raw_state_keys
      )
    )

    p <- hmm$plot("obspar", cov_safe, i = par_id) +
      geom_point(data = obs_df,
                 aes(x = x, y = y, fill = state, col = state),
                 alpha = 0.3) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = plot_colours,
                          labels = plot_labels,
                          breaks = legend_breaks,
                          name   = "State") +
      scale_fill_manual  (values = plot_colours,
                          labels = plot_labels,
                          breaks = legend_breaks,
                          name   = "State") +
      labs(title = paste0(bdisp, " vs ", cov_disp),
           x = cov_disp,
           y = axis_label(bsafe))
    print(p)
  }
}
```

## 7.6 Coefficient forest plots (covariate-augmented models)

Forest-style plots of the linear-predictor coefficients with 95% CI.
Two panels: one for **observation-mean** coefficients (one per
biomarker), one for **transition-probability** coefficients (one per
covariate, faceted by transition).

Coefficients whose CI crosses zero are greyed out — they are
indistinguishable from "no effect" at the 95% level. Style adapted
from the supervisor's PRS plotting code.

This section runs only when `has_covariates == TRUE`. For spline terms
the per-basis coefficients are technically uninterpretable singly;
read effect direction via Section 7.5 plots and use this section only
to spot which terms have CI well away from zero.

```{r cov-coeff-setup, eval=has_covariates, echo=FALSE}
.coeff_n_resp <- length(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)
.coeff_obs_h  <- max(4, 2.2 * .coeff_n_resp + 1)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 10, fig.height = .coeff_obs_h)
```

```{r coefficient-plots-obs, eval=has_covariates}
# ---- 1) Observation-mean coefficients --------------------------------------
# Defensive guard: if somebody runs this chunk manually with no covariates,
# bail out cleanly instead of crashing downstream on an empty data frame.
if (!has_covariates) {
  cat("No covariates configured — coefficient plot skipped.\n")
} else {
ci_obs <- hmm$confint()$coeff_fe$obs

obs_df_full <- as.data.frame(ci_obs) |>
  rownames_to_column("param")

# Param naming convention:
#   MVN:        "z.mu<i>.state<s>.<term>"
#   indep norm: "<bsafe>.mean.state<s>.<term>"
# Parse out (response biomarker, state, term) and skip pure intercepts.

parse_obs_param <- function(param) {
  # Try MVN form first
  m <- regmatches(param, regexec("^z\\.mu(\\d+)\\.state(\\d+)\\.(.+)$", param))[[1]]
  if (length(m) == 4) {
    i_idx <- as.integer(m[2]); state <- as.integer(m[3]); term <- m[4]
    bsafe <- RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i_idx]
    return(list(bsafe = bsafe, state = state, term = term))
  }
  # Independent-normals form: try each response prefix
  for (i in seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)) {
    bsafe <- RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]
    pat   <- paste0("^", bsafe, "\\.mean\\.state(\\d+)\\.(.+)$")
    m <- regmatches(param, regexec(pat, param))[[1]]
    if (length(m) == 3) {
      return(list(bsafe = bsafe, state = as.integer(m[2]), term = m[3]))
    }
  }
  NULL
}

parsed <- lapply(obs_df_full$param, parse_obs_param)
keep   <- !vapply(parsed, is.null, logical(1))
obs_df <- obs_df_full[keep, , drop = FALSE]
obs_df$bsafe <- vapply(parsed[keep], `[[`, character(1), "bsafe")
obs_df$state_raw <- vapply(parsed[keep], `[[`, integer(1),  "state")
obs_df$term  <- vapply(parsed[keep], `[[`, character(1), "term")

# Convert raw state index to the clinical (display) ordering
obs_df$state <- state_remap[obs_df$state_raw]

# Drop intercepts (they are part of the model but not a "covariate effect")
obs_df <- obs_df[obs_df$term != "(Intercept)", ]

# Display labels: replace safe covariate names inside the term string
for (j in seq_along(OBS_COVARIATES)) {
  obs_df$term <- gsub(OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE[j], OBS_COVARIATES[j],
                      obs_df$term, fixed = TRUE)
}

obs_df$bdisp      <- vapply(obs_df$bsafe, display, character(1))
obs_df$state_lbl  <- factor(state_levels[obs_df$state], levels = state_levels)
obs_df$cross_zero <- with(obs_df, lcl <= 0 & ucl >= 0)
obs_df$y_label    <- with(obs_df, paste0(term, "  (", state_lbl, ")"))

# Per-biomarker ordering of y axis so within each facet coefficients are
# sorted by mle (small-to-large bottom-to-top after the rev())
obs_df <- obs_df |>
  group_by(bdisp) |>
  arrange(mle, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(y_label = factor(y_label, levels = unique(y_label))) |>
  ungroup()

# state_colours is the canonical palette built in section 1.1; use it here.

ggplot(obs_df, aes(x = mle, y = y_label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lcl, xmax = ucl,
                     colour = ifelse(cross_zero, "cross zero",
                                     as.character(state_lbl))),
                 height = 0.2, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = ifelse(cross_zero, "cross zero",
                                 as.character(state_lbl))),
             size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ bdisp, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("cross zero" = "grey70", state_colours),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  labs(title = "Observation-mean coefficients (β with 95% CI)",
       subtitle = "Greyed out: CI crosses zero. One facet per response biomarker.",
       x = "Coefficient β",
       y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"))
}  # end defensive-guard else
```

```{r coefficient-plots-tpm, eval=has_covariates, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
if (!has_covariates) {

ci_tpm <- hmm$confint()$coeff_fe$hid
```

# 8. Estimated Parameters Summary

```{r param-summary}
if (has_covariates) {
  cat("Linear-predictor coefficients on observation parameters",
      "(intercepts + slopes per state):\n\n")
  print(round(hmm$coeff_fe()$obs, 3))
  cat("\n\nFor reference, observation parameters at the first data row",
      "(t = 1) are shown below in clinical units.\n\n")
}

obs_par <- hmm$par()$obspar[, , 1]   # rows = params, cols = states (raw)
# Permute columns to clinical state order
obs_par <- obs_par[, state_remap_inv, drop = FALSE]
colnames(obs_par) <- state_levels

# ── back-transform & build display table ────────────────────────────────
if (IS_a_MVN) {
  n_vars <- length(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)

  # Correlation row names use upper.tri convention (X < Y): corr12,
  # corr13, ..., corr_{p-1,p}. Build them in the same order hmmTMB uses.
  corr_idx <- which(upper.tri(matrix(0, n_vars, n_vars)), arr.ind = TRUE)
  corr_idx  <- corr_idx[order(corr_idx[, 1], corr_idx[, 2]), , drop = FALSE]

  expected_mu   <- paste0("z.mu",   seq_len(n_vars))
  expected_sd   <- paste0("z.sd",   seq_len(n_vars))
  expected_corr <- paste0("z.corr", corr_idx[, 1], corr_idx[, 2])

  # ── back-transform means and sds in-place ─────────────────────────────
  # to_clinical()    : undo z-score then expm1 (if log1p-flagged)
  # to_clinical_sd() : undo z-score (multiplicative) then lognormal-
  #                    variance formula when log1p-flagged; needs
  #                    mu_logscale = model-scale mean (before z-inversion)
  for (i in seq_len(n_vars)) {
    bsafe  <- RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]
    mu_row <- expected_mu[i]
    sd_row <- expected_sd[i]
    if (mu_row %in% rownames(obs_par)) {
      mu_model <- obs_par[mu_row, ]           # log-scale mean for sd formula
      obs_par[mu_row, ] <- to_clinical(obs_par[mu_row, ], bsafe)
      if (sd_row %in% rownames(obs_par))
        obs_par[sd_row, ] <- to_clinical_sd(obs_par[sd_row, ], bsafe,
                                            mu_logscale = mu_model)
    }
  }

  # ── assemble rows in the order: mean_i, sd_i, then all corr ──────────
  # Order: mu1, sd1, mu2, sd2, ..., muP, sdP, corr12, corr13, ...
  ordered_rows <- c(
    as.vector(rbind(expected_mu, expected_sd)),   # interleave mean/sd
    expected_corr
  )
  present      <- intersect(ordered_rows, rownames(obs_par))
  obs_par_sub  <- obs_par[present, , drop = FALSE]

  # ── human-readable row labels ─────────────────────────────────────────
  label_mu   <- paste0(RESPONSE_VARS, " — mean")
  label_sd   <- paste0(RESPONSE_VARS, " — sd")
  label_ms   <- as.vector(rbind(label_mu, label_sd))   # interleaved
  label_corr <- apply(corr_idx, 1, function(idx)
    paste0("corr(", RESPONSE_VARS[idx[1]], ", ", RESPONSE_VARS[idx[2]], ")"))

  all_labels  <- c(label_ms, label_corr)
  all_keys    <- c(as.vector(rbind(expected_mu, expected_sd)), expected_corr)
  rownames(obs_par_sub) <- all_labels[match(present, all_keys)]

} else {
  # ── independent-normals branch ────────────────────────────────────────
  # Back-transform each biomarker's mean and sd, then reorder rows to
  # mean_i / sd_i pairs and rename for display.
  n_vars <- length(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)

  for (i in seq_len(n_vars)) {
    bsafe    <- RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]
    mean_row <- paste0(bsafe, ".mean")
    sd_row   <- paste0(bsafe, ".sd")
    if (mean_row %in% rownames(obs_par)) {
      mu_model <- obs_par[mean_row, ]
      obs_par[mean_row, ] <- to_clinical(obs_par[mean_row, ], bsafe)
      if (sd_row %in% rownames(obs_par))
        obs_par[sd_row, ] <- to_clinical_sd(obs_par[sd_row, ], bsafe,
                                            mu_logscale = mu_model)
    }
  }

  # Interleave mean / sd rows per biomarker
  mean_rows <- paste0(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE, ".mean")
  sd_rows   <- paste0(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE, ".sd")
  ordered_rows <- as.vector(rbind(mean_rows, sd_rows))
  present      <- intersect(ordered_rows, rownames(obs_par))
  obs_par_sub  <- obs_par[present, , drop = FALSE]

  # Display names
  label_mean <- paste0(RESPONSE_VARS, " — mean")
  label_sd   <- paste0(RESPONSE_VARS, " — sd")
  all_labels <- as.vector(rbind(label_mean, label_sd))
  all_keys   <- as.vector(rbind(mean_rows, sd_rows))
  rownames(obs_par_sub) <- all_labels[match(present, all_keys)]
}

# ── Tidy per-state clinical mean/sd (drives Table A, heatmap, forest) ────────
# obs_par_sub rows are "<display> — mean" / "<display> — sd" (interleaved) and,
# for MVN, "corr(<i>, <j>)"; columns are states in display order. We keep the
# clean (un-escaped) rownames here and read the numbers straight out.
state_cols  <- colnames(obs_par_sub)           # state_levels in display order
header_cols <- unname(state_colours[state_cols])
em_dash     <- " — "                            # same dash used in the labels

escape_latex <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("(\\d+)\\^(\\d+)", "$\\1^{\\2}$", x, perl = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("_",  "\\\\_", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("%",  "\\\\%", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}

get_par_row <- function(bd, suffix) {
  key <- paste0(bd, em_dash, suffix)
  if (key %in% rownames(obs_par_sub)) as.numeric(obs_par_sub[key, ])
  else rep(NA_real_, length(state_cols))
}

param_tidy <- do.call(rbind, lapply(RESPONSE_VARS, function(bd) {
  ri <- ref_mean_sd(bd)
  data.frame(
    biomarker = bd,
    state     = factor(state_cols, levels = state_cols),
    mean      = get_par_row(bd, "mean"),
    sd        = get_par_row(bd, "sd"),
    lln       = if (is.null(ri)) NA_real_ else ri$lln,
    uln       = if (is.null(ri)) NA_real_ else ri$uln,
    row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

# ── Table A: one row per biomarker, cell = "mean (sd)" + out-of-range flag ───
flag_of <- function(mu, lln, uln) {
  if (is.na(mu)) return("")
  if (!is.na(lln) && mu < lln) return(" $\\downarrow$")
  if (!is.na(uln) && mu > uln) return(" $\\uparrow$")
  ""
}
tableA <- data.frame(Biomarker = escape_latex(RESPONSE_VARS),
                     check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for (st in state_cols) {
  tableA[[st]] <- vapply(RESPONSE_VARS, function(bd) {
    r <- param_tidy[param_tidy$biomarker == bd & as.character(param_tidy$state) == st, ]
    if (nrow(r) == 0 || is.na(r$mean)) return("")
    paste0(sprintf("%.3g (%.2g)", r$mean, r$sd), flag_of(r$mean, r$lln, r$uln))
  }, character(1))
}
tableA[["Normal range"]] <- vapply(RESPONSE_VARS, function(bd) {
  ri <- ref_mean_sd(bd)
  if (is.null(ri)) "" else sprintf("[%.3g, %.3g]", ri$lln, ri$uln)
}, character(1))

tbl <- knitr::kable(
  tableA,
  format    = "latex",
  booktabs  = TRUE,
  escape    = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE,
  align     = c("l", rep("c", length(state_cols)), "c"),
  caption   = paste0(
    if (IS_a_MVN) "Estimated MVN" else "Estimated",
    " state-dependent parameters",
    if (has_covariates) " at $t=1$ (intercepts only)" else "",
    " in clinical units. Cell = mean (sd); $\\downarrow$/$\\uparrow$ mark a state ",
    "mean below/above the normal range. Correlations are shown in the heatmap below."
  )
) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"),
    full_width    = FALSE
  )

for (j in seq_along(state_cols)) {
  tbl <- tbl |>
    kableExtra::column_spec(j + 1L,
      color = header_cols[j],
      bold  = TRUE)
}

tbl
```

## 8.1 State-dependent correlations (MVN)

```{r param-corr-heatmap, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.6, eval=IS_a_MVN}
if (IS_a_MVN && exists("corr_idx") && nrow(corr_idx) > 0) {
  corr_tidy <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(corr_idx)), function(k) {
    i <- corr_idx[k, 1]; j <- corr_idx[k, 2]
    lab <- paste0("corr(", RESPONSE_VARS[i], ", ", RESPONSE_VARS[j], ")")
    if (!(lab %in% rownames(obs_par_sub))) return(NULL)
    vals <- as.numeric(obs_par_sub[lab, ])
    rbind(
      data.frame(state = state_cols, v1 = RESPONSE_VARS[i], v2 = RESPONSE_VARS[j], corr = vals),
      data.frame(state = state_cols, v1 = RESPONSE_VARS[j], v2 = RESPONSE_VARS[i], corr = vals)
    )
  }))
  diag_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(RESPONSE_VARS, function(v)
    data.frame(state = state_cols, v1 = v, v2 = v, corr = 1)))
  corr_tidy <- rbind(corr_tidy, diag_df)
  corr_tidy$state <- factor(corr_tidy$state, levels = state_cols)
  corr_tidy$v1    <- factor(corr_tidy$v1,    levels = RESPONSE_VARS)
  corr_tidy$v2    <- factor(corr_tidy$v2,    levels = rev(RESPONSE_VARS))

  ggplot(corr_tidy, aes(v1, v2, fill = corr)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", corr)), size = 2.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ state, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b",
                         midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "corr") +
    labs(title = "State-dependent correlations (MVN emission)", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
          panel.grid  = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right")
} else {
  cat("No MVN correlations to display.\n")
}
```

# 9. Model Checking

## 9.1 Pseudo-residuals

Under a correctly specified model, pseudo-residuals are iid $N(0,1)$. The
QQ-plot diagnoses distributional fit and the ACF plot diagnoses temporal
dependence not captured by the latent state process.

### Univariate case

For independent normals hmmTMB ships `pseudores()`, which we use directly.

### Multivariate (MVN) case

`hmmTMB::pseudores()` does not support `mvnorm`, so we compute the
**ordinary pseudo-residuals** (Zucchini, MacDonald & Langrock 2017,
§6.2.2) by hand, using a per-biomarker marginal:

$$
z_{it} \;=\; \Phi^{-1}\!\big(\Pr(X_{it} \le x_{it} \mid X_{(-it)})\big)
$$

with

$$
\Pr(X_{it} \le x_{it} \mid X_{(-it)})
\;=\;
\frac{\tilde\alpha(t{-}1)\,\Gamma\,\mathrm{diag}\!\big(F_{i,s}(x_{it})\big)\,\tilde\beta(t)^{\!\top}}
     {\tilde\alpha(t{-}1)\,\Gamma\,\tilde\beta(t)^{\!\top}}
$$

where

- $\tilde\alpha, \tilde\beta$ are the **scaled forward/backward** vectors,
  computed under the *full MVN joint density* $\mathcal N_p(\mathbf x_t;\,
  \mu_s,\,\Sigma_s)$ for each state — scaling prevents underflow and makes
  the ratio invariant, so the normalising constants cancel;
- $F_{i,s}$ is the **marginal** CDF of biomarker $i$ in state $s$, i.e.
  $\mathcal N(\mu_{i,s}, \sigma_{i,s})$, extracted from the MVN by the
  standard property that the marginal of a multivariate Normal on
  coordinate $i$ is univariate Normal with the same mean and variance
  $(\Sigma_s)_{ii}$ — the off-diagonal entries integrate out;
- at $t = 1$ we use the initial distribution $\delta$ in place of
  $\tilde\alpha(0)\,\Gamma$;
- forward/backward are restarted independently for each patient (each
  `ID` is an independent time series).

Note this is the *proper* forward/backward-based pseudo-residual — not a
posterior-weighted CDF via `state_probs()`, which would condition on
$X_{it}$ itself and defeat the purpose of a residual diagnostic.

```{r pseudo-residuals-helpers}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Forward/backward recursions for one patient, with row-sum scaling
# (Zucchini, MacDonald & Langrock 2017, §3.2 / §4.1).
#
# Returns scaled alpha-tilde and beta-tilde such that the normalising
# constants drop out of the numerator/denominator ratio in §6.2.2.
#
# Crucially, the per-row state likelihood P[t, s] = f_s(x_t) is the
# *full multivariate* MVN density N_p(x_t; mu_s, Sigma_s), NOT the
# product of the univariate marginals. This is what makes the resulting
# pseudo-residual "the marginal pseudo-residual of the MVN" rather than
# "the pseudo-residual of an independent-normals model": marginals are
# used only inside F_{i,s}, while forward/backward use the joint density.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
forward_backward_patient <- function(x_obs, Gamma, delta, mu, Sigma_list) {
  Ti <- nrow(x_obs)                      # length of this patient's series
  K  <- nrow(Gamma)                      # number of latent states

  # P[t, s] = f_s(x_t) = N_p(x_t; mu_s, Sigma_s), the joint MVN density.
  # mvtnorm::dmvnorm with log = TRUE then exp() keeps things stable
  # before the row-sum scaling below.
  P <- matrix(NA_real_, Ti, K)
  for (s in seq_len(K)) {
    P[, s] <- exp(mvtnorm::dmvnorm(x_obs,
                                   mean  = mu[s, ],
                                   sigma = Sigma_list[[s]],
                                   log   = TRUE))
  }

  # Forward pass with scaling: alpha_tilde[t] sums to 1 at each t,
  # c_t collects the per-step normalising constants.
  alpha <- matrix(0, Ti, K); c_t <- numeric(Ti)
  phi        <- delta * P[1, ]                          # alpha_1 ∝ δ ⊙ f(x_1)
  c_t[1]     <- sum(phi)
  alpha[1, ] <- phi / c_t[1]
  for (t in 2:Ti) {
    phi        <- (alpha[t - 1, ] %*% Gamma) * P[t, ]   # α̃_{t-1} Γ ⊙ f(x_t)
    c_t[t]     <- sum(phi)
    alpha[t, ] <- phi / c_t[t]
  }

  # Backward pass with the same scaling convention. Setting beta_T to
  # 1 / c_T (rather than 1) makes the products α̃_t β̃_t cancel the c_t
  # factors cleanly when forming the conditional probabilities.
  beta <- matrix(0, Ti, K)
  beta[Ti, ] <- 1 / c_t[Ti]
  for (t in (Ti - 1):1) {
    b           <- Gamma %*% (P[t + 1, ] * beta[t + 1, ])
    beta[t, ]   <- as.numeric(b) / c_t[t]
  }

  list(alpha = alpha, beta = beta, c_t = c_t, P = P)
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract per-state means, marginal sds, and *full* covariance matrices
# Sigma_s from the fitted hmmTMB object.
#
# hmmTMB stores MVN parameters under the list-column name `z` with rows:
#   z.mu1 ... z.muP        (means)
#   z.sd1 ... z.sdP        (marginal sds = sqrt of diagonal of Sigma)
#   z.corr<X><Y>           (correlations, X < Y, upper-triangle convention)
#
# For the independent-normals branch the convention is different
# (<bm_safe>.mean / <bm_safe>.sd, no correlations), so we dispatch on
# is_mvn. In the independent case Sigma_s collapses to diag(sd^2).
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
extract_state_params <- function(hmm_obj, response_vars_safe, is_mvn) {
  obs_par <- hmm_obj$par()$obspar[, , 1]
  K <- N_STATES
  p <- length(response_vars_safe)

  mu <- sd <- matrix(NA_real_, K, p)
  for (i in seq_len(p)) {
    if (is_mvn) {
      mu_row <- paste0("z.mu", i); sd_row <- paste0("z.sd", i)
    } else {
      mu_row <- paste0(response_vars_safe[i], ".mean")
      sd_row <- paste0(response_vars_safe[i], ".sd")
    }
    mu[, i] <- obs_par[mu_row, ]
    sd[, i] <- obs_par[sd_row, ]
  }

  # Build Sigma_s for each state: D R D, where D = diag(sd_s) and R is
  # the correlation matrix. In the independent case R = I and Sigma_s
  # stays diagonal.
  Sigma_list <- vector("list", K)
  for (s in seq_len(K)) {
    R <- diag(p)                                   # correlation matrix
    if (is_mvn && p >= 2) {
      # Upper-triangle iteration matches hmmTMB's z.corr<X><Y> naming
      # (X < Y); see CLAUDE.md note on upper.tri vs lower.tri pitfall.
      idx <- which(upper.tri(R), arr.ind = TRUE)
      for (k in seq_len(nrow(idx))) {
        i <- idx[k, 1]; j <- idx[k, 2]
        corr_row <- paste0("z.corr", i, j)
        rho <- obs_par[corr_row, s]
        R[i, j] <- R[j, i] <- rho
      }
    }
    D  <- diag(sd[s, ], nrow = p)
    Sigma_list[[s]] <- D %*% R %*% D               # Sigma_s = D R D
  }

  list(mu = mu, sd = sd, Sigma_list = Sigma_list)
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stationary distribution as a fallback for delta when hmm$hid()$delta()
# is not exposed. Solves delta (Γ − I) = 0 subject to 1ᵀ delta = 1 via
# the augmented least-squares system, so we get a unique solution even
# when Γ − I is rank-deficient (it is, by construction).
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
get_initial_delta <- function(hmm_obj, Gamma) {
  d <- tryCatch(hmm_obj$hid()$delta(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(d)) {
    d <- as.numeric(d)
    if (length(d) == N_STATES) return(d / sum(d))
  }
  K <- nrow(Gamma)
  A <- rbind(t(Gamma - diag(K)), rep(1, K))
  b_vec <- c(rep(0, K), 1)
  as.numeric(solve(t(A) %*% A, t(A) %*% b_vec))
}
```

```{r pseudo-residuals, fig.height=8, cache=TRUE}
# Diagnostic panels: QQ against N(0,1) for distributional fit, ACF for
# residual temporal dependence the latent chain failed to absorb.
qq_panel <- function(res, name) {
  ggplot(data.frame(res = res), aes(sample = res)) +
    stat_qq(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.7) +
    stat_qq_line(colour = "red") +
    labs(title = paste("QQ:", name), x = "Theoretical", y = "Sample")
}

acf_panel <- function(res, name, lag.max = 14) {
  ac <- acf(res, plot = FALSE, na.action = na.pass, lag.max = lag.max)
  ci <- 1.96 / sqrt(sum(!is.na(res)))
  data.frame(lag = as.numeric(ac$lag[-1]),
             acf = as.numeric(ac$acf[-1])) |>
    ggplot(aes(lag, acf)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-ci, ci),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "blue") +
    geom_segment(aes(xend = lag, yend = 0)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:lag.max) +
    labs(title = paste("ACF:", name), x = "Lag (days)", y = "ACF")
}

if (IS_a_MVN) {
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # MVN branch: implement Zucchini §6.2.2 by hand.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  Gamma  <- hmm$par()$tpm[, , 1]                   # transition matrix Γ
  delta  <- get_initial_delta(hmm, Gamma)          # initial distribution δ
  pars   <- extract_state_params(hmm, RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE, is_mvn = TRUE)
  mu     <- pars$mu                                # K × p means
  sd_mat <- pars$sd                                # K × p marginal sds
  Sigmas <- pars$Sigma_list                        # list of K full Σ_s

  K   <- N_STATES
  p   <- length(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)
  eps <- .Machine$double.eps^0.5                   # clipping for qnorm()

  pr_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(hmm_data), ncol = p)
  colnames(pr_mat) <- RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE

  # Forward/backward is restarted independently for each patient (each
  # ID is an independent time series under the model).
  for (id in levels(hmm_data$ID)) {
    idx <- which(hmm_data$ID == id)
    x   <- as.matrix(hmm_data[idx, RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE, drop = FALSE])
    Ti  <- nrow(x)
    if (Ti < 1) next

    # Run the scaled forward/backward under the full MVN joint density.
    fb <- forward_backward_patient(x, Gamma, delta, mu, Sigmas)

    # ag[t, ] = α̃(t-1) Γ, with the convention ag[1, ] = δ in place of
    # α̃(0) Γ (the t = 1 boundary condition in Zucchini §6.2.2). Using
    # ag instead of α̃(t) is what makes the resulting probability
    # *exclude* x_t from the conditioning set, i.e. produces an
    # *ordinary* (not smoothed) pseudo-residual.
    ag <- matrix(0, Ti, K)
    ag[1, ] <- delta
    if (Ti >= 2) for (t in 2:Ti) ag[t, ] <- fb$alpha[t - 1, ] %*% Gamma

    # Denominator of the pseudo-residual ratio:
    #   α̃(t-1) Γ β̃(t)ᵀ  =  Σ_s [α̃(t-1) Γ]_s · β̃_s(t)
    # Computed once per t and shared across biomarkers. Negative or
    # zero values would indicate numerical degeneracy (a near-impossible
    # observation under the model); flag them as NA.
    denom <- rowSums(ag * fb$beta)
    denom[denom <= 0] <- NA_real_

    # Loop over biomarkers. For each i we plug the *univariate marginal*
    # CDF F_{i,s} = Φ((x − μ_{i,s}) / σ_{i,s}) into the diagonal of the
    # numerator quadratic form, then form the conditional probability
    # and map it through Φ⁻¹.
    for (i in seq_len(p)) {
      # F_mat[t, s] = F_{i,s}(x_{it}). The marginal of an MVN on
      # coordinate i is N(μ_{i,s}, σ_{i,s}) — off-diagonals integrate
      # out, so pnorm() is exact for the marginal CDF (we are NOT
      # approximating by ignoring correlations here; the marginal is
      # genuinely univariate Normal).
      F_mat <- vapply(seq_len(K),
        function(s) pnorm(x[, i], mean = mu[s, i], sd = sd_mat[s, i]),
        numeric(Ti))

      # Numerator: α̃(t-1) Γ diag(F_{i,s}(x_{it})) β̃(t)ᵀ
      #         =  Σ_s [α̃(t-1) Γ]_s · F_{i,s}(x_{it}) · β̃_s(t)
      numer <- rowSums(ag * F_mat * fb$beta)

      # Conditional CDF, clipped away from 0/1 so that qnorm() returns
      # finite values even for grossly mis-modelled observations
      # (saturated residuals appear as ±~5.6 in the QQ-plot).
      p_cond <- pmin(pmax(numer / denom, eps), 1 - eps)

      # Normal pseudo-residual z_{it} = Φ⁻¹(p_cond). Under H_0 of a
      # correctly specified model, these are iid N(0, 1).
      pr_mat[idx, i] <- qnorm(p_cond)
    }
  }

  plots_pr <- c(
    lapply(seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE),
           function(i) qq_panel (pr_mat[, RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]],
                                 RESPONSE_VARS[i])),
    lapply(seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE),
           function(i) acf_panel(pr_mat[, RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]],
                                 RESPONSE_VARS[i]))
  )
} else {
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Independent-normals branch: hmmTMB's pseudores() handles this case
  # natively. Forward/backward under independence factorises exactly
  # over biomarkers, so the library implementation is exact — no need
  # to re-derive.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  pr <- hmm$pseudores()
  plots_pr <- c(
    lapply(seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE),
           function(i) qq_panel (pr[[RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]]],
                                 RESPONSE_VARS[i])),
    lapply(seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE),
           function(i) acf_panel(pr[[RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]]],
                                 RESPONSE_VARS[i]))
  )
}

wrap_plots(plots_pr, ncol = 2)
```

```{r save-fig-pseudoresiduals, echo=FALSE}
         width = 10, height = 8)
```

# 10. State-occupancy patterns

How many patients stay in a single state for their entire admission, and
how many transition between states? This sets up the population split
exploited by the post-hoc notebook (`hmm_posthoc.Rmd`):

- **Stayers** → used to characterise each state's "central population"
  via depth measures (Section 1 in posthoc).
- **Switchers** → analysed as their own subgroup (Section 2 in posthoc).

## 10.1 Stayers vs switchers — counts

```{r stayer-counts}
patient_states <- hmm_data |>
  group_by(ID) |>
  summarise(
    n_states_visited = n_distinct(state),
    # state is a factor with levels = state_levels (in clinical order),
    # so as.integer(state) gives the new state index 1..N directly.
    state_sequence   = paste(as.integer(state), collapse = "->"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    pattern = if_else(n_states_visited == 1, "stayer", "switcher"),
    sole_state = if_else(
      n_states_visited == 1,
      state_levels[as.integer(sub("->.*", "", state_sequence))],
      NA_character_
    )
  )

cat("Stayer / switcher split:\n")
print(table(patient_states$pattern))

cat("\nStayer breakdown by state:\n")
print(table(patient_states$sole_state, useNA = "no"))

cat("\nNumber of distinct states visited (per patient):\n")
print(table(patient_states$n_states_visited))
```

## 10.2 Alluvial diagram of state sequences

For visual clarity we collapse each patient's day-by-day state sequence
to its **transition checkpoints**: day 0, day 7, day 14. Patients are
grouped by the (S_0, S_7, S_14) triplet. Stayers form a single straight
flow, switchers branch.

```{r alluvial-all, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# Lazy-install ggalluvial only if needed

CHECKPOINT_DAYS <- c(0, 7, 14)

alluvial_df <- hmm_data |>
  filter(time %in% CHECKPOINT_DAYS) |>
  select(ID, time, state) |>
  mutate(time_lbl = factor(paste0("Day ", time),

# Counts of (Day0, Day7, Day14) trajectories
alluvial_wide <- alluvial_df |>
  select(-time) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = time_lbl, values_from = state) |>
  count(`Day 0`, `Day 7`, `Day 14`, name = "Freq")

ggplot(

) +

       subtitle = paste0("Checkpoints: days ",

                         ". Strip width \u221d patient count."),
       x = NULL, y = "Number of patients") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

# 11. Uncertainty quantification (final model)

`hmm$confint()$coeff_fe` is necessary but not sufficient on its own. It
returns intervals for the fixed-effect coefficients $\alpha$ on the
**working (link) scale**, from `TMB::sdreport()`. Three consequences:

* For the state-dependent **means** the link is the identity and the model is
  covariate-free, so the intercept interval *is* the interval for
  $\mu_{j}$ — on the z-score scale. It still has to be pushed through the
  z-score and `log1p` back-transform to be reported in clinical units.
  Both maps are monotone, so the endpoints transform directly.
* For the **standard deviations** (log link) and the **correlations**
  (tanh-type link) the same monotone-endpoint argument applies.
* For the **transition probabilities** it does not. What `coeff_fe$hid`
  contains is the multinomial-logit coefficients $\eta_{jk}$, and
  $\gamma_{jk} = e^{\eta_{jk}} / (1 + \sum_{l \neq j} e^{\eta_{jl}})$ depends
  on the whole row. A marginal interval for $\eta_{jk}$ is therefore *not* an
  interval for $\gamma_{jk}$: the transformation is neither monotone in a
  single coefficient nor free of the others. The same applies to everything
  derived from $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}$, in particular the stationary
  distribution $\boldsymbol{\pi}$, which Section 7.4 reports as a point
  estimate only.

hmmTMB solves this with `HMM$predict(what, n_post = ...)`, which draws from
the approximate distribution of the parameters and returns intervals for the
quantity itself: `"obspar"`, `"tpm"` and `"delta"` (the stationary
distribution). Both are reported below: the raw coefficients for
completeness, and the interpretable-scale intervals for the thesis tables.

```{r uq-config}
N_POST <- 1000     # posterior draws used for the interpretable-scale intervals
```

## 11.1 Working-scale coefficients

```{r uq-coeff-fe}
ci_fe <- tryCatch(hmm$confint(), error = function(e) {
  warning("hmm$confint() failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

if (!is.null(ci_fe)) {
  fe_obs <- as.data.frame(ci_fe$coeff_fe$obs) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("parameter")
  fe_hid <- as.data.frame(ci_fe$coeff_fe$hid) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("parameter")
  save_tab(fe_obs, "tab09_uq_coeff_fe_obs",
           caption = "Observation-model fixed effects, working (link) scale, with 95% Wald intervals.")
  save_tab(fe_hid, "tab10_uq_coeff_fe_hid",
           caption = paste0("Hidden-process fixed effects: multinomial-logit ",
                            "coefficients eta_jk, working scale. These are NOT ",
                            "intervals for gamma_jk; see Section 11.2."))
}
```

## 11.2 Intervals on the interpretable scale

```{r uq-predict}
# hmmTMB has returned the point estimate under either `mle` or `mean`
# depending on version; accept both, and fail loudly if neither is there.
pick <- function(x, nm = "mean") {
  if (!is.list(x))
    stop("hmm$predict() returned an array, not a list: n_post was ignored.")
  v <- x[[nm]]
  if (is.null(v)) v <- x[["mle"]]
  if (is.null(v)) stop("No point estimate found in hmm$predict() output; ",
                       "names are: ", paste(names(x), collapse = ", "))
  v
}

# t = 1 is essential. Without it, and with no newdata, hmmTMB predicts at
# every row of the data set: with N_POST draws that is nrow(hmm_data) x N_POST
# evaluations and an array that will not fit in memory. The model is
# covariate-free, so all time points carry identical parameters and t = 1 is
# not an approximation.
# The draws are random: seeding them is what makes the reported intervals
# reproducible across knits.
safe_predict <- function(what) {
  tryCatch({
    set.seed(SEED)
    hmm$predict(what, t = 1, n_post = N_POST)
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning("hmm$predict(\"", what, "\", t = 1, n_post = ", N_POST,
            ") failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })
}

pred_obs <- safe_predict("obspar")
pred_tpm <- safe_predict("tpm")
pred_del <- safe_predict("delta")

cat("predict('obspar') returned : ",
    if (is.null(pred_obs)) "FAILED" else paste(names(pred_obs), collapse = ", "), "\n",
    "predict('tpm')    returned : ",
    if (is.null(pred_tpm)) "FAILED" else paste(names(pred_tpm), collapse = ", "), "\n",
    "predict('delta')  returned : ",
    if (is.null(pred_del)) "FAILED" else paste(names(pred_del), collapse = ", "), "\n",
    sep = "")

if (is.null(pred_obs) || is.null(pred_tpm))
  warning("Section 11.2 could not be computed. Do NOT report Sections 3.5/3.6 ",
          "of the chapter with intervals until this is fixed.")
```

### State-dependent parameters, clinical units

```{r uq-obspar}
if (!is.null(pred_obs)) {
  cat("predict('obspar') components:\n")
  for (nm in names(pred_obs))
    cat("  ", nm, ": dim = ",
        paste(dim(pred_obs[[nm]]) %||% length(pred_obs[[nm]]), collapse = " x "),
        "\n", sep = "")

  uq_done <- tryCatch({

    canon <- rownames(hmm$par()$obspar[, , 1])   # z.mu1, z.sd1, z.corr12, ...

    # Coerce whatever predict() returned into a [parameter x state] matrix,
    # tolerating 2-d or 3-d layouts, a transposed layout, and missing dimnames.
    to_mat <- function(a, nm) {
      if (is.null(a)) stop("component '", nm, "' is missing")
      d <- dim(a)
      m <- if (is.null(d))            matrix(as.numeric(a), nrow = length(a))
           else if (length(d) == 2)   unclass(as.matrix(a))
           else if (length(d) == 3)   a[, , 1]
           else stop("component '", nm, "' has ", length(d), " dimensions")
      m <- as.matrix(m)
      if (nrow(m) == N_STATES && ncol(m) == length(canon)) m <- t(m)
      if (ncol(m) != N_STATES || nrow(m) != length(canon))
        stop("component '", nm, "' is ", nrow(m), "x", ncol(m),
             ", expected ", length(canon), "x", N_STATES)
      rownames(m) <- canon
      m <- m[, state_remap_inv, drop = FALSE]
      colnames(m) <- state_levels
      m
    }

    tidy <- function(m, value_name)
      tibble::as_tibble(m, rownames = "parameter") |>
        tidyr::pivot_longer(-parameter, names_to = "state", values_to = value_name)

    uq_all <- tidy(to_mat(pick(pred_obs), "estimate"), "est") |>
      dplyr::left_join(tidy(to_mat(pred_obs$lcl, "lcl"), "lcl"),
                       by = c("parameter", "state")) |>
      dplyr::left_join(tidy(to_mat(pred_obs$ucl, "ucl"), "ucl"),
                       by = c("parameter", "state")) |>
      dplyr::mutate(state = factor(state, levels = state_levels))

    # ---- means and standard deviations, clinical units ----------------------
    uq_obs <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE), function(i) {
      bsafe <- RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]
      mu <- dplyr::filter(uq_all, parameter == paste0("z.mu", i))
      sd <- dplyr::filter(uq_all, parameter == paste0("z.sd", i))
      mu <- dplyr::arrange(mu, state); sd <- dplyr::arrange(sd, state)
      tibble::tibble(
        biomarker = RESPONSE_VARS[i],
        state     = mu$state,
        mean      = to_clinical(mu$est, bsafe),
        mean_lcl  = to_clinical(mu$lcl, bsafe),
        mean_ucl  = to_clinical(mu$ucl, bsafe),
        sd        = to_clinical_sd(sd$est, bsafe, mu_logscale = mu$est),
        sd_lcl    = to_clinical_sd(sd$lcl, bsafe, mu_logscale = mu$est),
        sd_ucl    = to_clinical_sd(sd$ucl, bsafe, mu_logscale = mu$est))
    })

    save_tab(uq_obs, "tab11_uq_state_parameters_clinical",
             caption = paste0("Final model: state-dependent means and standard ",
                              "deviations in clinical units, with 95% intervals from ",
                              N_POST, " posterior draws. Endpoints are transformed ",
                              "individually, which is valid because both maps are ",
                              "monotone; the sd interval holds the mean at its point ",
                              "estimate and is therefore conditional on mu-hat."))

    # ---- correlations -------------------------------------------------------
    p_resp <- length(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)
    if (p_resp >= 2) {
      idx <- which(upper.tri(matrix(0, p_resp, p_resp)), arr.ind = TRUE)
      uq_corr <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(idx)), function(r) {
        a <- idx[r, 1]; b <- idx[r, 2]
        rn <- paste0("z.corr", a, b)
        d  <- dplyr::filter(uq_all, parameter == rn)
        if (nrow(d) == 0) return(NULL)
        tibble::tibble(
          pair  = paste(RESPONSE_VARS[a], RESPONSE_VARS[b], sep = " - "),
          state = d$state, rho = d$est, lcl = d$lcl, ucl = d$ucl,
          excludes_zero = sign(d$lcl) == sign(d$ucl))
      })
      if (!is.null(uq_corr) && nrow(uq_corr) > 0) {
        save_tab(uq_corr, "tab11b_uq_state_correlations", digits = 4,
                 caption = paste0("Final model: state-dependent correlations with ",
                                  "95% intervals from ", N_POST, " posterior draws."))
        cat("\nCorrelations whose interval excludes zero: ",
            sum(uq_corr$excludes_zero), " of ", nrow(uq_corr), "\n", sep = "")
      } else {
        warning("predict('obspar') returned no correlation rows.")
      }
    }

    # ---- figure -------------------------------------------------------------
    p_uq_mu <- ggplot(uq_obs, aes(mean, state, colour = state)) +
      geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = mean_lcl, xmax = mean_ucl), height = 0.18) +
      geom_point(size = 2.4) +
      facet_wrap(~ biomarker, scales = "free_x") +
      scale_colour_manual(values = state_colours, guide = "none") +
      labs(title = "State-dependent means with 95% intervals",
           subtitle = "Clinical units; final model", x = NULL, y = NULL)
    print(p_uq_mu)
    save_fig(p_uq_mu, "fig20_uq_state_means", width = 10, height = 4)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning("Section 11.2 (obspar) failed: ", conditionMessage(e),
            " -- tab11/tab11b/fig20 not produced.")
    FALSE
  })
}
```

### Transition probabilities and stationary distribution

```{r uq-tpm}
uq_tpm_done <- tryCatch({
  if (is.null(pred_tpm)) stop("predict('tpm') returned nothing")

  grab <- function(a, nm) {
    if (is.null(a)) stop("component '", nm, "' is missing")
    d <- dim(a)
    m <- if (length(d) == 3) a[, , 1] else as.matrix(a)
    if (!identical(dim(m), c(as.integer(N_STATES), as.integer(N_STATES))))
      stop("component '", nm, "' is ", paste(dim(m), collapse = "x"),
           ", expected ", N_STATES, "x", N_STATES)
    m[state_remap_inv, state_remap_inv, drop = FALSE]
  }
  g_est <- grab(pick(pred_tpm), "estimate")
  g_lcl <- grab(pred_tpm$lcl, "lcl")
  g_ucl <- grab(pred_tpm$ucl, "ucl")

  uq_tpm <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(state_levels), function(j)
    tibble::tibble(from = state_levels[j], to = state_levels,
                   gamma = g_est[j, ], lcl = g_lcl[j, ], ucl = g_ucl[j, ]))
  save_tab(uq_tpm, "tab12_uq_transition_probabilities", digits = 4,
           caption = paste0("Final model: transition probabilities with 95% ",
                            "intervals from ", N_POST, " posterior draws."))

  uq_dwell <- tibble::tibble(
    state      = state_levels,
    gamma_jj   = diag(g_est),
    dwell_days = 1 / (1 - diag(g_est)),
    dwell_lcl  = 1 / (1 - diag(g_lcl)),
    dwell_ucl  = 1 / (1 - diag(g_ucl)))
  save_tab(uq_dwell, "tab13_uq_expected_dwell_times", digits = 3,
           caption = paste0("Final model: expected dwell times in days, with the ",
                            "intervals induced by those on gamma_jj. Compare with ",
                            "the ", dplyr::n_distinct(hmm_data$time),
                            "-day observation window."))
  TRUE
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("Section 11.2 (tpm) failed: ", conditionMessage(e),
          " -- tab12/tab13 not produced."); FALSE
})

uq_delta_done <- tryCatch({
  if (is.null(pred_del)) stop("predict('delta') returned nothing")
  first_col <- function(a, nm) {
    if (is.null(a)) stop("component '", nm, "' is missing")
    v <- if (is.null(dim(a))) as.numeric(a) else {
      m <- as.matrix(a)
      if (nrow(m) == N_STATES) as.numeric(m[, 1])
      else if (ncol(m) == N_STATES) as.numeric(m[1, ])
      else stop("component '", nm, "' has no margin of length ", N_STATES)
    }
    v[seq_len(N_STATES)]
  }
  d_est <- first_col(pick(pred_del), "estimate")[state_remap_inv]
  d_lcl <- first_col(pred_del$lcl, "lcl")[state_remap_inv]
  d_ucl <- first_col(pred_del$ucl, "ucl")[state_remap_inv]

  if (exists("pi_stat")) {
    disc <- max(abs(d_est - as.numeric(pi_stat)))
    cat("Max |predict('delta') - Section 7.4 pi| = ", signif(disc, 3), "\n", sep = "")
    if (disc > 1e-3)
      warning("predict('delta') disagrees with Section 7.4; one is mis-permuted.")
  }

  uq_delta <- tibble::tibble(state = state_levels, pi = d_est,
                             lcl = d_lcl, ucl = d_ucl)
  save_tab(uq_delta, "tab14_uq_stationary_distribution", digits = 4,
           caption = "Final model: stationary distribution with 95% intervals.")

  p_uq_pi <- uq_delta |>
    dplyr::mutate(state = factor(state, levels = state_levels)) |>
    ggplot(aes(state, pi, fill = state)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), width = 0.15) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = state_colours) +
    labs(title = "Stationary distribution with 95% intervals",
         x = NULL, y = "Probability")
  print(p_uq_pi)
  save_fig(p_uq_pi, "fig21_uq_stationary_distribution", width = 7, height = 4.5)
  TRUE
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("Section 11.2 (delta) failed: ", conditionMessage(e),
          " -- tab14/fig21 not produced."); FALSE
})
```

> **What kind of intervals these are.** Both `confint()` and the draws behind
> `predict(n_post = )` come from the same source: the normal approximation to
> the distribution of the fixed-effect parameters produced by
> `TMB::sdreport()`. They are Wald-type, not bootstrap, and they inherit the
> caveat that the hmmTMB authors state for the Laplace approximation, namely
> that it can behave poorly when the likelihood is multimodal or markedly
> asymmetric. Section 5.1 is the relevant check: if the restarts all reach
> the same maximum, the approximation is on safer ground. Report the
> intervals as asymptotic.
>
> **Still open.** The intervals above are conditional on the fitted model:
> they quantify parameter uncertainty, not uncertainty from the choice of
> $K$, from the response set, or from the fact that the observations are
> GAM-smoothed trajectories rather than measurements. If you also want
> decoding uncertainty (the entropy of the smoothed state probabilities, or
> the share of patient-days whose maximum posterior probability falls below a
> threshold) or a patient-level bootstrap, say so and I will add it; neither
> is implemented here.

---

# 12. Export fitted objects for post-hoc analysis

`hmm_posthoc.Rmd` reuses these objects without refitting. The bundle keeps
the previous schema so the post-hoc notebook does not need editing, with two
changes: there is no held-out set any more, and the provenance of the model
selection is recorded alongside the fit.

```{r export-objects}
posthoc_bundle <- list(
  # Fitted model + working data
  hmm        = hmm,
  hmm_data   = hmm_data,                 # all rows, with Viterbi states
  test_data  = NULL,                     # no hold-out in this design
  df_full    = df,                       # safe-renamed columns + covariates
  # Split indices (kept for schema compatibility)
  train_ids  = levels(hmm_data$ID),
  test_ids   = character(0),
  # Configuration
  config     = list(
    RESPONSE_VARS        = RESPONSE_VARS,
    RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE   = RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE,
    OBS_COVARIATES       = OBS_COVARIATES,
    OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE  = OBS_COVARIATES_SAFE,
    COVARIATE_TERMS      = if (exists("COVARIATE_TERMS")) COVARIATE_TERMS else NULL,
    SPLINE_K_DEFAULT     = if (exists("SPLINE_K_DEFAULT")) SPLINE_K_DEFAULT else NULL,
    SPLINE_BS            = if (exists("SPLINE_BS")) SPLINE_BS else NULL,
    N_STATES             = N_STATES,
    APPLY_ZSCORE         = APPLY_ZSCORE,
    IS_a_MVN             = IS_a_MVN,
    SEED                 = SEED,
    TEST_FRAC            = TEST_FRAC,
    DATA_PATH            = DATA_PATH,
    BM_LOG1P_DECISIONS_PATH = BM_LOG1P_DECISIONS_PATH,
    CATEGORICAL_COVS     = CATEGORICAL_COVS,
    STATE_LABELS_MAP        = if (exists("STATE_LABELS_MAP"))     STATE_LABELS_MAP     else NULL,
    STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER     = if (exists("STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER"))  STATE_DISPLAY_ORDER  else NULL,
    STATE_PALETTE_CUSTOM    = if (exists("STATE_PALETTE_CUSTOM")) STATE_PALETTE_CUSTOM else NULL,
    USE_CUSTOM_STATE_LABELS = USE_CUSTOM_STATE_LABELS
  ),
  # Provenance of the model-selection stages (summaries only; the candidate
  # fits themselves are deliberately not carried forward)
  selection  = list(
    axis_stems          = AXIS_STEMS,
    axis_under_test     = AXIS_UNDER_TEST,
    K_axis_test         = K_AXIS_TEST,
    K_grid              = K_GRID,
    K_final             = N_STATES,
    ovl_drop_threshold  = OVL_DROP_THRESHOLD,
    min_state_share_pct = MIN_STATE_SHARE_PCT,
    stage1_metrics      = stage1_metrics,
    stage1_overlap      = stage1_overlap,
    stage2_criteria     = stage2_criteria,
    stage2_overlap      = stage2_overlap,
    stage2_occupancy    = stage2_occupancy,
    spec_cohort_file    = SPEC_DATA_PATH,
    final_cohort_file   = DATA_PATH
  ),
  # Name mapping
  name_map   = list(
    display_to_safe = display_to_safe,
    safe_to_display = safe_to_display
  ),
  # State decoding output
  patient_states = patient_states,
  # Back-transform metadata
  needs_expm1    = needs_expm1,
  zscore_params  = zscore_params,
  # Clinical state remap artefacts
  state_remap     = state_remap,
  state_remap_inv = state_remap_inv,
  state_levels    = state_levels,
  state_colours   = state_colours,
  state_palette   = unname(state_colours)
)

saveRDS(posthoc_bundle, file = "hmm_fit_objects_tesi4.rds")
cat("Saved fitted-model bundle to hmm_fit_objects_tesi4.rds\n")
cat("Object size on disk: ",
    round(file.info("hmm_fit_objects_tesi4.rds")$size / 1024^2, 2), " MB\n", sep = "")
```
